# Story Studio KH — Changelog

What's new in each release. Newest first.

---

## v1.0.628 — 2026-07-16

**Production jobs now preserve every verified prompt and media result before reporting completion.**

- Kept Scene Plan visual and motion prompts checkpointed independently by stable scene ID, with visible per-pack saved counts and manual Retry limited to missing or duplicated prompts.
- Verified scene images, motion clips, compositions, and image-pool outputs from authoritative files before allowing their jobs to finish; valid partial results remain available for recovery.
- Prevented an accepted Studio Hub batch from falling back to duplicate provider work during a temporary monitoring outage, and required cancellation acknowledgement on stop or timeout.
- Added a queue-level Retry fallback so every failed or cancelled job can be re-enqueued with its exact durable parameters even before a page-specific recovery control exists.
- Disabled hidden SDK retries for paid OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic requests while retaining bounded automatic retries for verified local/free work.
- Added clearer Scene Plan, Scene Review, Motion Review, and publishing job labels, filters, cancellation feedback, and smart-retry explanations.
- Added regression coverage for partial prompt/media checkpoints, Hub reconnection and cancellation, retry parameter preservation, and paid-provider one-shot policy.

## v1.0.627 — 2026-07-16

**Scene Plan now proves every prompt checkpoint independently before a pack or job can finish.**

- Re-read the authoritative saved Scene Plan after every LLM pack and reported the exact durable count, such as 17/20, instead of treating the provider call as all-or-nothing.
- Continued later packs after a partial cloud response while keeping every valid visual or motion prompt already saved by stable scene ID.
- Made final completion use the on-disk prompt audit, so incomplete jobs fail loudly and manual Retry requests only missing or duplicated scene IDs.
- Hardened YouTube publishing checkpoints so a completed upload ID survives optional thumbnail or playlist failures and cannot be accidentally uploaded twice after a crash.
- Verified playlist membership before spending insert quota and checkpointed thumbnail, schedule, and playlist updates without overwriting one another.
- Added regression coverage for partial prompt packs, disk-verified completion, crash-safe upload identity, deferred resumable cleanup, and provider mutation checkpoints.

## v1.0.626 — 2026-07-16

**One failed Scene Plan result no longer blocks valid prompts in the same batch.**

- Checkpointed every returned scene row independently for direct cloud and Studio Hub prompt packs.
- Continued saving later valid rows when one scene ID is unexpected, malformed, or temporarily cannot be written.
- Let the shared completion audit inspect the authoritative saved Scene Plan so partial Hub jobs report the exact remaining scene IDs.
- Kept paid-provider safety intact: cloud work is never auto-retried, and manual Retry requests only prompts that are still missing or duplicated.
- Added regression coverage for mid-pack checkpoint failures and unexpected provider scene IDs.

## v1.0.625 — 2026-07-16

**Every Scene Plan prompt path now preserves completed work scene by scene.**

- Extended locked, atomic prompt checkpoints to bulk visual repair, bulk motion repair, and the retired planner's remaining motion pass so a later failure cannot discard earlier results.
- Re-read the saved Scene Plan before reporting completion instead of trusting in-memory worker counts.
- Kept incomplete jobs visibly failed while making Retry target only scene IDs that are still missing or duplicated.
- Rejected unexpected provider scene IDs before they can modify a different scene.
- Hardened expression-markup generation to save each completed chapter independently and reject tag output that omits, rewords, or reorders narration.
- Added regression coverage for concurrent expression checkpoints, dialect changes, narration integrity, truncated prompt JSON, and concurrent prompt saves.

## v1.0.624 — 2026-07-16

**Scene prompts and media now checkpoint independently without losing completed work.**

- Kept each valid visual or motion prompt durable as soon as its stable scene ID returns, even when another result in the same LLM pack is missing or malformed.
- Continued later prompt packs after a partial response while leaving the overall job visibly incomplete and making Retry request only missing scene IDs.
- Centralized scene image and motion-clip registration behind one locked, atomic Scene Plan checkpoint so concurrent jobs cannot overwrite each other.
- Verified every downloaded image and clip is a non-empty file before linking it into Scene Review, and failed loudly if its stable scene disappeared.
- Removed best-effort media registration paths that could leave paid results on disk but invisible to the app.
- Added regression coverage for truncated prompt responses, concurrent prompt and media saves, empty files, missing scenes, and clip metadata.

## v1.0.623 — 2026-07-16

**Scene Plan prompts now survive incomplete LLM packs one result at a time.**

- Atomically checkpointed every visual and motion prompt by stable scene ID as soon as it is returned.
- Preserved complete rows from truncated cloud JSON instead of discarding an otherwise useful response.
- Continued processing later prompt packs when an earlier pack is incomplete, while failing the final job for the exact missing IDs.
- Made manual Retry submit only prompts still missing from the authoritative Scene Plan and prevented Hub fallback from repeating saved work.
- Added live per-pack saved counts and regression coverage for partial, concurrent, empty, and truncated prompt results.

## v1.0.622 — 2026-07-16

**Studio Hub scene images are now saved durably as each render finishes.**

- Routed completed image artifacts through Studio Hub's authenticated proxy instead of exposing raw fleet-worker links to Story Studio.
- Saved every image atomically and updated its stable Scene Plan record before advancing job progress.
- Retried transient per-item save failures five times and surfaced a blocking error if persistence still fails instead of silently discarding completed work.
- Removed best-effort Scene Plan writes that could leave generated PNGs invisible in Scene Review.
- Recovered all 101 existing EP0037 images from Studio Hub without regenerating or spending credits.

## v1.0.621 — 2026-07-16

**Qwen3 cloned voices now flow through one fleet-wide Studio Hub library.**

- Loaded canonical cloned voices from Studio Hub first, with direct Voice Studio discovery retained only as a compatibility fallback.
- Preserved each Hub voice's stable identity in presets and generation requests so the selected clone is never confused with a same-named local voice.
- Routed Hub-owned voices back through Studio Hub even when an older local routing preference still says Direct.
- Fixed Qwen Base models being mistaken for the Qwen CustomVoice preset-speaker model simply because they share a model family.
- Updated the audited Qwen3 safe request threshold from 2,000 to 3,000 characters while preserving deliberately customized limits.

## v1.0.620 — 2026-07-16

**Cloud scene prompt packs no longer lose their output budget to hidden reasoning.**

- Disabled OpenRouter reasoning for deterministic Scene Plan prompt packs so visible prompts receive the full response budget.
- Enabled provider-native JSON mode for direct cloud scene packs, preventing malformed structured responses from silently dropping scene IDs.
- Captured provider finish reasons and token usage so incomplete jobs can distinguish output truncation from invalid JSON.
- Clarified in Scene Plan that the response budget is separate from the model's much larger input/context window.
- Preserved paid-call safety: valid partial prompts remain saved and manual Retry submits only missing scene IDs without automatically spending credits again.

## v1.0.619 — 2026-07-16

**Audio chapters can now be sent to TTS one at a time.**

- Added an inline Generate action to every Audio Generator chapter row.
- Ensured inline generation submits only that chapter through the existing confirmation, provider, queue, and completion path.
- Disabled conflicting row actions while the episode already has an audio job in flight and respected regeneration mode for completed chapters.
- Added responsive row controls and regression coverage for exact one-chapter dispatch.

## v1.0.618 — 2026-07-16

**Current Kie image pricing and safe Qwen voice cloning are now available.**

- Added Kie.ai Nano Banana 2 Lite and Seedream 5 Pro with their current image tiers, request parameters, and cost estimates.
- Limited the built-in image catalog to the supported Qwen Z-Image, Grok, Seedream, Nano Banana, and GPT Image 2 families.
- Fixed image generation so the selected resolution tier controls both the displayed price and the provider request.
- Applied the recorded GenAIPro, fal.ai, ElevenLabs direct, and kie.ai TTS rates, including the corrected ElevenLabs v3 direct price.
- Added Qwen3-TTS Base 0.6B and 1.7B voice-cloning models while updating the built-in Qwen CustomVoice model.
- Kept cloned voices on the Voice Studio server that owns their local voice ID instead of allowing Studio Hub to route them to an incompatible server.
- Made Voice Studio job polling recover from brief server restarts without resubmitting completed speech generation.

## v1.0.607 — 2026-07-15

**Pipeline stage selection is now explicit and safer.**

- Added **Required stages** to select the current chain without optional Research or paid Motion Clips.

- Added regression coverage to prevent stages from silently returning to an all-selected default.

## v1.0.605 — 2026-07-15

**Production Board now opens focused on episodes that still need work.**

## v1.0.604 — 2026-07-15

**Phase 5 unifies the remaining assembly and library workspaces, with one shared Channel Characters system.**

- Replaced separate project and global character workflows with one **Channel Characters** workspace backed by a canonical shared record.
- Added channel labels and independent provider-aware voice profiles, so the same character can use a different voice and delivery for each channel.

## v1.0.603 — 2026-07-15

**Studio Hub connection setup is now explicit, verifiable, and clear about fleet routing.**

- Reworked Local Models → Studio Hub into one connection card with a visible **Save & test connection** action, persistent Saved/Unsaved feedback, and a separate test for the stored connection.
- Clarified that loopback Story Studio connections need no access token: Studio Hub owns the private credential used to reach remote workers.
- Added a fleet-authentication readiness check without exposing the Hub's secret and reports rejected remote Hub credentials with an actionable status.
- Made the routing contract visible: Hub mode sends work to Studio Hub first, while direct sibling URLs are emergency fallback only when the Hub itself is unreachable.
- Pairs with Studio Hub 1.37.1, which routes remote generation through each machine's connected peer Hub so stale worker credentials cannot fail an entire batch.

## v1.0.602 — 2026-07-15

- Fixed rich Image and Voice Studio catalogs being clipped by Scene Review and other cards by placing them above the workspace in a viewport-aware floating layer.
- Unified LLM, image, TTS, image-to-video, and transcription pickers across generators, reviews, style previews, vision analysis, expression markup, and B-Roll tools.
- Removed the format wizard's stale hardcoded paid-model list so it now restores a live usable model through the shared inventory.
- Added regression coverage for model-menu accessibility, viewport placement, media-type coverage, and prevention of hardcoded paid defaults.

## v1.0.601 — 2026-07-15

**The complete writing and thumbnail flow now shares one calm, modern creation workspace.**

- Added clear creative-purpose headers, live episode and job context, and compact readiness metrics without changing any generation behavior.
- Standardized preset and episode controls inside one command surface so the six pages no longer shift between unrelated toolbar layouts.

## v1.0.600 — 2026-07-15

**Large production workspaces now stay responsive without weakening authoritative asset checks.**

- Added shared request coalescing and safe caching for stable project settings, active formats, and model inventories, with precise save-time invalidation and protection against stale in-flight responses.

- Made Scene Review and Motion Review progressively reveal large scene collections while deferring off-screen image and video loading until it is useful.
- Prevented stale episode responses and overlapping Motion Review polling from replacing current workspace state during navigation or slow fleet responses.
- Reduced repeated Production Board completion scans, parallelized API-key inventory reads, and shortened the interactive Studio Hub model timeout while preserving direct-studio fallback.
- Made clearing completed Job Queue history update immediately even when project storage is on a slow synchronized volume.
- Added regression coverage for stable shared caches, mutation invalidation, stale-read protection, progressive scene mounting, and deferred media loading.

- Modernized Pipeline with a production summary, dedicated command surface, consistent stage sections, clearer batch scope, and shared preflight and blocking notices.
- Modernized Production Board with a unified control-room header, visible episode and stage metrics, a compact responsive command bar, and a raised matrix surface while preserving its fast row virtualization.
- Reorganized Scene Plan into clear prerequisite, configuration, execution, and scene-editor regions without changing deterministic timing, prompt batching, opening visuals, or repair behavior.
- Brought Motion Review onto the shared review shell with consistent guidance notices and readiness hierarchy while preserving external uploads, still-image decisions, image-to-video generation, and back-to-top navigation.

## v1.0.597 — 2026-07-15

**The first shared Story Studio workspace design system now unifies every workflow family.**

- Added a centralized responsive design layer for page heroes, section hierarchy, notices, context metrics, control sizing, motion preferences, and compact-window behavior.
- Added reusable Workspace Hero, Workspace Section, and Workspace Notice components so future pages inherit the same visual language instead of recreating it in scoped CSS.
- Modernized the shared Top Action Bar used by fifteen generation and assembly pages with named regions, consistent sizing, clearer grouping, and a full-width compact action state.
- Migrated Audio Generator, Scene Review, Subtitles, and Job Queue as the representative Generator, Review, Assembly, and Management workspaces without changing their generation behavior.
- Replaced several page-specific warnings with one consistent, actionable status pattern and made job context and episode readiness visible in the page header.
- Added regression coverage that keeps all four workflow families on the shared page shell and protects responsive and reduced-motion support.

## v1.0.596 — 2026-07-15

**Cancelling fleet generation now requires Studio Hub to acknowledge the stop.**

- Replaced fire-and-forget Hub cancellation with a bounded, three-attempt acknowledgement request for generation and durable Chat batches.
- Keeps the local job classified as cancelled while surfacing a clear warning if Studio Hub cannot confirm the cancellation, rather than silently leaving remote work running.
- Encodes the exact Hub batch ID and preserves fleet authentication on every cancellation request.
- Pairs with Studio Hub 1.37.0, which immediately forwards cancellation to running Studio worker job IDs and exposes safe image-queue cleanup controls.
- Added regression coverage for acknowledged cancellation, exact batch routing, and refused Hub cancellation.

## v1.0.595 — 2026-07-15

**Automatic scene-image retries now repair only the images that are still missing.**

- Fixed Generate All Missing carrying its original scene list into every automatic retry and resubmitting already completed images to Studio Hub.
- Re-checks the unified and legacy scene-image folders before each retry, then builds a new Hub batch containing only scene IDs that remain absent.
- Reports the actual repair batch size on each attempt instead of restarting progress at the original full scene count.
- Keeps manual Regenerate Selected behavior unchanged, so an intentional re-render can still replace existing chosen images.
- Added regression coverage for partial missing-only recovery, explicit selected regeneration, and ordinary resume behavior.

## v1.0.594 — 2026-07-15

**Scene Review and Pipeline now share one scene-image render queue.**

- Unified Scene Review's Generate All Missing action with the Pipeline's canonical continuity renderer instead of creating a separate `scene_images_batch` workload.
- Preserved Studio Hub fleet batching, adaptive parallel dispatch, verified partial-output recovery, prompt-only mode, render size, and concurrency settings through the shared renderer.
- Added cross-type queue ownership so an older Scene Review batch already queued or running is reused instead of submitting duplicate scene images to Studio Hub.
- Lets a Pipeline join an existing manual scene render and continue its remaining steps exactly once after that render completes.
- Shows the reused Job ID in Scene Review and reports reused renders clearly when a Pipeline starts.
- Added regression coverage for cross-type deduplication, Pipeline continuation handoff, and protection against replacing another Pipeline's continuation.

## v1.0.593 — 2026-07-15

**Scene and Motion Review are clearer, calmer, and much easier to navigate.**

- Rebuilt both review headers with visible workflow context, stronger hierarchy, and a modern review-focused visual treatment.
- Reorganized Scene Review into separate readiness, render-settings, and review-action zones instead of one overflowing mixed toolbar.
- Refined scene rows, thumbnails, action alignment, progress feedback, empty states, and responsive behavior across desktop and compact windows.
- Modernized Motion Review with clearer optional-step guidance, external-clip instructions, readiness progress, model controls, and balanced image-to-video cards.
- Fixed Scene Review's existing back-to-top control watching the wrong dashboard container, then added the same labeled floating control to Motion Review.
- The back-to-top control now appears after a useful scroll distance, stays clear of row actions, and returns smoothly to the workspace header.

## v1.0.592 — 2026-07-15

**YouTube publishing now has a thumbnail-first review and predictable scheduling.**

- Rebuilt the Upload Center around a modern publishing desk with channel, ready-episode, uploaded-library, plan, and queue status at a glance.
- Added a full thumbnail picker inside Upload preview, including a large inspection view, every available episode thumbnail, pinned-default labels, and an unmistakable selected state.
- Carries the exact chosen thumbnail into fresh uploads and metadata-only updates without changing the episode's saved default.
- Validates thumbnail filenames and episode ownership before queueing, then re-verifies the exact file during execution instead of silently falling back to a different image.
- Normalizes multi-episode schedule selections into natural episode order regardless of checkbox click order or request order.
- Makes schedule preview and apply share the same authoritative episode-to-slot assignments and clearly shows when scheduling continues after the latest existing upload.
- Added regression coverage for deterministic schedule ordering, duplicate selection healing, and thumbnail path/traversal rejection.

## v1.0.591 — 2026-07-14

**Free local pipeline work now repairs transient failures automatically without risking paid API spend.**

- Added two bounded automatic retries for proven-local Voice Studio subtitles and TTS, Image Studio generation, Chat Studio text work, deterministic timeline work, local assembly, and local B-Roll processing.
- Preserves every verified partial output between attempts, so subtitle retries fill only missing chapter SRTs and generation retries skip completed items.
- Keeps cloud, paid, free-tier API, cloud-proxied Chat Studio, YouTube, and unknown future providers manual-only through a deny-by-default policy.
- Removed hidden cloud completion and paid Kie TTS resubmission loops; safe polling, provider-history recovery, and finished-file downloads remain resilient without creating another generation task.
- Added live Job Queue feedback for retry countdowns, attempt numbers, recovered work, and exhausted local retries.
- Prevents Pipeline chaining until a recovered job passes the same verified-completion audit as its original attempt.
- Added regression coverage for partial local subtitle recovery, cloud subtitle one-shot behavior, local provider classification, and uncertain paid submission responses.

## v1.0.590 — 2026-07-14

**Video Assembly is now one Scene Plan-driven workflow on this Mac or Render Studio.**

- Removed the retired Timestamp Assembly page, renderer, route, job type, Pipeline step, preset surface, navigation tabs, and stale build artifacts.
- Made the approved Scene Plan the only authority for scene identity, order, image or motion choice, exact duration, opening reservation, and merged audio.
- Added a visible timing panel with plan/audio totals, still and motion counts, uncovered or overlapping time, a proportional timeline, and expandable exact scene rows.
- Blocks enqueue and execution when any required scene is missing, unapproved, stale, uncovered, overlapping, or detached from merged audio, while naming the exact repair needed.
- Browser and preset payloads can no longer reorder, exclude, shuffle, recycle, or substitute scenes; the server rehydrates current authoritative inputs before every render.
- Routed the same unified `video_assembly` job through Studio Hub to Render Studio when the chosen editing controls have lossless worker support, with checksum and media verification before completion.
- Updated Render Studio to advertise the unified Video Assembly and Scene Plan timing capabilities and reject retired workflow payloads.
- Added regression coverage for unified prerequisites, strict Scene Plan asset selection, worker eligibility, stale-input healing, and retired-flow removal.

## v1.0.589 — 2026-07-14

**Manual step completion now updates immediately and proves the saved state.**

- Added visible Updating feedback while a step chip or Production Board cell is being marked done.
- Updates the shared episode status immediately, then performs a mutation-safe refresh so the step count, pending list, selector, and Production Board stay in sync.
- Prevents an older in-flight episode request from overwriting a newly saved manual completion.
- Keeps the selected episode visible in Pending only long enough to show the completed chip and refreshed count.
- Validates the backend response and refreshed episode before showing success instead of treating a completed request as proof that the override persisted.
- Added manual completion support for current optional steps including Research, Subtitles, Character Sheet, Scene Plan, Scene Review, Motion Review, and B-Roll selection.
- Added regression coverage for stale-request races and the complete current override allowlist.

## v1.0.588 — 2026-07-14

**Video generation and final assembly now use the Studio fleet.**

- Connected Story Studio to Video Studio's live image-to-video catalog through Studio Hub, with authenticated direct fallback when the Hub is unreachable.
- Kept provider credentials, paid-use controls, model availability, pricing, and retirement inside Video Studio instead of duplicating them into project settings.
- Replaced editable project video models with a read-only, refreshable live catalog showing cloud/local lane, clip limit, and provider price.
- Routed the current six-step continuity Video Assembly through Render Studio when the selected features have lossless worker equivalents; unsupported advanced layers stay local and name the reason in the Job log.
- Added exact source-image transfer, hardware-worker preference, intro reservation, scene motion, subtitles, presentation framing, post-audio tails, and checksum-verified result return to the worker recipe.
- Strengthened remote completion so a returned render must contain video and audio streams, cover the expected duration, and land under the canonical final filename before the job reports Done.
- Added regression coverage for image-to-video-only model discovery and safe Render Studio eligibility/fallback behavior.

## v1.0.587 — 2026-07-14

**Presets are now one clear local list with no device or cloud scope.**

- Removed the confusing **This device / All devices** preset switch, machine-origin labels, cross-device warnings, and the retired machine-label API.
- Preserved every existing preset from both old device scopes and merged them into the same local project list instead of hiding or deleting any.
- Automatically strips obsolete machine-origin metadata when presets are loaded and when the preset store is next saved.
- Kept Audio and Video Assembly file-integrity checks, so missing intro, music, frame, logo, or overlay files still block safely with direct replacement actions.
- Updated the Presets workspace and import contracts to describe the local-only model consistently.
- Added regression coverage preventing device/cloud preset scopes from returning.

## v1.0.586 — 2026-07-14

**Notifications is now a compact control center with clearer setup and safer saving.**

- Added an at-a-glance readiness summary for Desktop alerts, Telegram, and the daily production brief.
- Replaced the long Telegram walkthrough with a three-step setup that masks the bot token, detects the user's chat, and verifies delivery with a test message.

## v1.0.562 — 2026-07-13

**One-click completion is now verified from the full expected output set instead of inferred from partial files or a worker returning normally.**

- Added a shared completion contract: multi-item jobs save successful partial work, fail loudly with exact missing/invalid items, and remain safely retryable rather than showing a green Done badge.
- Hardened script expansion, introductions, prompts, metadata, research, images, audio, clips, B-Roll, repairs, scene planning, and final assembly against empty, short, corrupt, or partial results.
- Added durable expected-count manifests for scene prompts, thumbnail prompts, metadata, and merged audio, preventing partial documents from shrinking the downstream definition of “complete.”
- Production Board and Pipeline status now validate real output content, unique Scene Plan prompts, complete subtitles, non-empty images/clips, and canonical final videos; legacy folder scanning can no longer override an authoritative incomplete result.
- Every declared job type must have a queue lane and executor. Startup and regression tests now fail when a future module is added without complete one-click wiring.
- Final render naming is consistent across local, B-Roll, timestamp, and Render Studio assembly, and YouTube Upload only accepts that canonical verified final instead of guessing among preview files.
- Added a permanent Verified Completion Contract to the project instructions so new features must ship with failure, retry, status, and partial-output regression coverage.

## v1.0.561 — 2026-07-13

**Partial transcription jobs now fail loudly instead of showing a misleading green Done badge.**

- Every per-chapter transcription run performs a final on-disk audit against all sections in `audio_chapters.json`.
- A provider error, zero-cue response, empty audio file, or absent chapter now produces a red Failed job naming every missing section.
- Successfully transcribed chapters remain saved; Retry skips those files and fills only the remaining gaps.
- The success summary now reports verified ready sections, newly generated sections, and new cue count instead of claiming all chapters completed when one failed.
- Whole-episode tracks cannot mask missing per-chapter source files during this strict post-job audit.

## v1.0.560 — 2026-07-13

**Pending Subtitles now means every expected narration section is actually covered.**

- Replaced the old “any subtitle file exists” shortcut with chapter-aware completion against `audio_chapters.json`.
- Partial stitched tracks no longer hide missing chapters; their verified metadata identifies exactly which sections are covered and which remain pending.
- Valid whole-episode Whisper, imported, chapter-marker, and verified stitched tracks remain supported.
- The Subtitles status display and episode selector now share the same completion result, preventing the visible chapter count and Pending list from disagreeing.
- Subtitle folders and the audio-section manifest are now watched by the episode cache, and the cache schema is refreshed so existing incorrect Done results self-heal after updating.
- Renamed or retitled episode folders resolve by episode code and their audio manifest, keeping subtitle detection attached to the real project folder.

## v1.0.559 — 2026-07-13

**Scene prompts must now be real, unique, and backed by complete narration before images or final video can render.**

- Removed obsolete “planner fallback” warnings from older deterministic timelines; opening Scene Plan or Scene Review safely cleans those stale labels without changing prompts, timings, or images.
- Exact duplicate visual prompts no longer count as completed work. The first remains valid, later copies return to the pending pool and are included by Next/All pending and prompt repair.
- Scene Review names missing and duplicated prompts, pauses image rendering, and links directly to the repair step instead of allowing repeated visuals into a finished episode.
- Missing subtitle chapters now block Scene Review, per-scene generation, fleet batches, continuity rendering, completion status, and final assembly at the backend as well as in the UI.
- Scene Plan and production status only mark the step complete when every prompt is unique and the stitched subtitle timeline verifies every audio section.
- Older numbered images from a superseded timeline are reported separately and intentionally left unmapped; the app never guesses which new stable scene ID they belong to.
- Verified the affected Dozing Knight plans: DK0035/36 contain unique prompts and only stale labels; DK0037/38 each contain four duplicate prompt copies that are now surfaced for repair.

## v1.0.558 — 2026-07-13

**Scene Plan can no longer hide missing chapter subtitles inside one extremely long scene.**

- Subtitle stitching now requires usable cues for every audio section and names each missing chapter instead of writing a misleading partial timeline.
- Older partial stitches are detected in Scene Plan; timeline rebuilds and prompt generation pause until the missing chapters are transcribed and stitched.
- The retired LLM scene-boundary Re-plan controls are removed. Older clients receive a clear retirement response instead of quietly starting the legacy workflow.
- Added deterministic “Repair long scenes”: after subtitles are restored, it splits only abnormal ranges against real cues while preserving all unaffected prompts, images, approvals, and stable scene IDs.
- Abnormal scenes that overlap missing subtitle audio now say “missing subtitle narration” and link directly to the Subtitles workspace.
- Fixed the floating Back to top button listening to the wrong page container, so it now appears during long Scene Plan scrolls.
- Added regression coverage for partial subtitle stitches and non-destructive long-scene repair.

## v1.0.557 — 2026-07-13

**Scene prompt batching now adapts to the selected model instead of forcing every provider into a 10-scene pack.**

- Local and free-cloud models remain capped at 10 scenes per request; paid cloud defaults to 20 and has a guarded maximum of 30.
- Output budgets adapt with the pack: 4,096 tokens for local/free cloud and 8,192 for paid cloud, with larger packs protected from an undersized manual budget.
- Scene Plan shows the effective tier, pack size, and output budget before generation, with an Advanced override that only offers 20/30 for paid cloud.
- Presets and one-click Pipeline retain the adaptive settings and model tier. Invalid or stale values self-heal to Automatic.
- Studio Hub receives and preserves the tier with each durable batch, while direct paid-cloud providers use the same pack policy and save completed stable scene IDs after every response.
- Fixed the manual Scene Plan route dropping its saved output-budget setting before the job was queued.

## v1.0.556 — 2026-07-13

**Audio presets can no longer leave out the Introduction.** Section checkboxes are episode-specific and are no longer stored inside reusable voice/model presets.

- Newly saved audio presets retain the voice, model, delivery, and generation settings without capturing the current episode's selected sections.
- One-click Pipeline audio always targets all narration sections. In Skip Existing mode, files already on disk are skipped and only missing sections are generated.

- Branded-opening presets also retain the selected 1–120 second reserve.
- One-click Pipeline runs receive the same saved opening settings, so manual Scene Plan and batch generation build identical timelines.

## v1.0.554 — 2026-07-13

**Scene prompts have adjustable output headroom, and Video Assembly now validates the real continuity timeline before rendering.**

- Asset scanning reports exact planned-image coverage, including the missing stable scene IDs, and Auto mode recognizes a Scene Plan even when no planned images have rendered yet.

## v1.0.553 — 2026-07-12

**Local visual-prompt packs now have enough output space to finish.** Ten full-detail prompts can no longer be silently squeezed into Chat Studio's 1,024-token default.

- Visual packs request 4,096 output tokens; optional motion packs request 2,048. Ten 110–150 word visual prompts now fit in one Hub response.
- Structured-output instructions explicitly prohibit reasoning, thought channels, markdown, and commentary before the JSON result.
- Reduced prompt temperature for more reliable scene IDs and JSON formatting.

- Studio Hub independently recovers complete scene objects from reasoning-prefixed or truncated responses, preserving partial work before retrying only missing IDs.

## v1.0.552 — 2026-07-12

**Scene Plan is now exactly three stages with one optional LLM choice.** There is no separate planning model because timeline creation is deterministic.

- Timeline sends no model and job logs explicitly identify it as deterministic with no LLM.
- A single selector, “Visual & motion prompt model,” drives both full-detail visual prompts and the optional motion-prompt pass.
- Removed the separate fast prompt-model control and the obsolete Advanced Planner section from Scene Plan.
- Visual and motion stages continue using durable Studio Hub packs of up to 10 scenes; motion remains completely optional.
- The research preference is now passed with visual-prompt jobs rather than the model-free timeline job.
- Per-scene repair actions remain available for exceptions but are not additional required workflow passes.

## v1.0.551 — 2026-07-12

**Scene Plan now shows only the controls that govern the staged workflow.** Timeline state, continuity pacing, full-detail prompting, and Hub batching are visible where the work happens.

- Build buttons become Rebuild buttons when a timeline already exists, and the confirmation repeats the last-built state before clearing prompts.

- Older empty-prompt plans retain an estimated build time when they resume; all newly built timelines store a dedicated timestamp that prompt updates cannot overwrite.
- Added regression coverage preventing legacy planner settings from returning through Pipeline presets.

## v1.0.550 — 2026-07-12

**Scene Plan completion is now truthful and self-healing.** A timestamp shell can no longer appear finished when visual-prompt generation failed or stopped partway through.

- Scene Plan is complete only when the plan contains scenes and every scene has a non-empty visual prompt; timeline-only and partially prompted plans stay pending.
- Scene Review cannot report complete before its required Scene Plan prompts are complete, even if image files happen to exist.
- The one-click Pipeline now creates the deterministic timeline and automatically continues through all required visual-prompt packs before advancing. A missing model or incomplete Hub batch fails visibly instead of producing a false success.
- Manual staged planning remains flexible: Timeline can be built by itself, Visual Prompts can resume only missing stable scene IDs, and Motion Prompts remain optional.
- Status caches are invalidated on upgrade so previously cached false positives, including DK0038's 273-scene plan with zero prompts, are recalculated immediately.
- Added regression coverage for empty and partially prompted plans.

## v1.0.549 — 2026-07-12

**Scene planning is now staged, durable, and aligned with short branded openings.** Long Introduction narration no longer forces a multi-minute title-card hold or delays story scenes until Chapter 1.

- Replaced whole-Introduction skipping with two explicit choices: reserve an exact branded opening window, or generate story visuals from the first second.
- After a branded opening, scenes immediately cover the remaining Introduction narration; prompt packs are instructed to depict the story premise instead of welcome, CTA, subscription, or breathing language.
- Scene timing is now a deterministic first stage with no LLM call. Visual prompts and optional motion prompts run as separate resumable stages.
- Local visual and motion work routes through Studio Hub's durable Chat queue in packs of up to 10 scenes per server. Ten available Chat Studio machines can process up to 100 prompts in one wave.
- Results are stitched and saved by stable scene ID, completed packs survive restarts, partial runs retain their results, and rerunning submits only pending scenes. Direct Chat Studio remains a connection-failure fallback.
- Video Assembly reads the opening duration saved in `scene_plan.json`, trims or pads the branded clip to that exact window, and blocks a render when the required clip is missing.
- Removed the legacy automatic thumbnail hold. A sequential title card is skipped when a branded opening owns the reserved window so scene timestamps cannot drift.
- Motion prompting defaults off for new projects and is clearly optional; still-image episodes remain complete and renderable.
- Added visible Hub task IDs in Scene Plan plus regression coverage for durable Chat submission, polling, authentication, stable-ID results, and fallback behavior.

## v1.0.548 — 2026-07-12

**Image repair now reports what it actually restored.** A completed provider-history check can no longer appear as a successful repair when no image was recovered.

- Repair jobs persist structured counts for restored files, fresh-generation gaps, and unrecoverable provider tasks; completion notifications use those outcomes instead of treating every finished check as success.
- The Image Integrity card shows each missing filename together with its provider task ID, or clearly says when no task ID was recorded.
- Free Repair is offered only for missing files with stored provider history. Files that were never submitted get a separate Generate Missing Fresh action that skips valid images and warns through the normal credit confirmation.
- The queued Story job ID is displayed immediately with a direct Jobs link, and the image list automatically rescans when repair finishes.
- Provider downloads are verified at the expected file path before they count as restored, with regression coverage for truthful completion messages and older repair logs.

## v1.0.547 — 2026-07-12

**Studio Hub is now the authoritative gateway for the complete local AI fleet.** Story Studio discovers models, checks availability, submits generation, and transcribes audio through one Hub address and credential; saved direct Studio URLs are emergency fallback only.

- Image, Voice, Chat, and Whisper model pickers now read Studio Hub's fleet-wide inventory instead of probing individual LAN/Tailscale endpoints in Hub mode.
- Whisper transcription uploads route through Studio Hub, which selects a free Voice Studio Mac with the requested model downloaded.
- Whisper model downloads broadcast through Studio Hub to compatible Voice Studio machines.
- Direct Image, Voice, and Chat fallback traffic now shares one authenticated `X-Studio-Token` request layer, including catalogs, generation, polling, cancellation, and protected artifacts.
- Image catalog capabilities and downloaded state merge across the fleet, so a sleeping first-listed Mac can no longer hide models available elsewhere.
- Chat's dedicated and global model pickers now use Hub inventory, while direct Chat completions receive fleet authentication when fallback is required.
- Added regression coverage for Hub inventory conversion, fleet download-state merging, stable Voice model IDs, and shared fleet-token behavior.

## v1.0.546 — 2026-07-12

**Performance defaults are consistent and gentler on provider APIs.** Every generation category now starts at 3 concurrent jobs, while image, audio, and video requests launch 2 seconds apart by default.

- Raised every launch-stagger control and runtime clamp from 5 seconds to 20 seconds for stricter provider limits.
- Existing saved values remain unchanged, including an explicit 0 ms to disable staggering; only unset settings receive the new defaults.
- Text, image, audio, video, and subtitle concurrency now default to 3. Subtitle Auto remains available for matching the live Voice Studio fleet.
- Centralized backend performance defaults and added regression tests so the settings screen and workers cannot silently drift apart.
- Concurrency can still be raised as high as 50, with corrected labels and clearer guidance to increase cautiously according to provider quota.

## v1.0.545 — 2026-07-12

**Long job names stay inside their cards.** Jobs with full chapter lists no longer push Stop, Cancel, Retry, or status controls beyond the window.

- Job status, type, and episode remain visible while long generated titles truncate safely with a hover tooltip for the full text.
- Action buttons keep a fixed trailing position instead of being displaced by job details.
- Cards, lists, and log output now constrain their own width; logs scroll internally rather than widening the page.
- Narrow windows wrap the action row below the job identity without overlap.

## v1.0.544 — 2026-07-12

**Voice Studio transcription recognizes protected fleet models again.** Story Studio now authenticates remote Voice Studio requests with the shared Studio Hub fleet credential.

- Fixed Whisper models appearing “not downloaded” even though Voice Studio reported them ready locally. Remote model probes were being rejected after Voice Studio added fleet-token protection.
- On the main Mac, Story Studio securely reads the credential from Studio Hub's loopback-only fleet endpoint; remote Story Studio installs can use their configured Hub token.
- The credential is attached to transcription availability, model downloads, transcription uploads, TTS generation, job polling, voice catalogs, and audio downloads.
- Token lookup is cached and deduplicated, while missing tokens retry quickly during Studio Hub startup.
- No separate transcription Pinokio app is required; Voice Studio remains the dedicated local transcription service.

## v1.0.543 — 2026-07-12

**Draft outlines can no longer inherit completion from older scripts.** Script completion now requires the current outline to be explicitly approved before any narration or chapter files can count as complete.

- Fixed DK0045's exact case: an unapproved 15-chapter outline was sitting over an older 12-chapter narration, but the older narration file made Script appear complete.
- Even when older files happen to match every slot in a new draft outline, the episode remains pending until that outline is approved and expanded.
- Invalidated episode-status cache again so existing false-positive completion marks are recomputed immediately after update.

## v1.0.542 — 2026-07-12

**Chapter expansion now proves completion and repairs partial runs.** A unified narration file is no longer enough to mark a known 15-chapter outline complete when only 12 chapter sources exist.

- Script completion now checks the approved outline's exact chapter count and reports partial expansions as pending.
- Expansion reconciles stale progress from chapter files on disk, preserving valid work after interruptions instead of regenerating it.
- One-click and full expansion runs retry missing chapters once, then fail clearly and remain resumable if any gap survives.
- Pipeline resumes approved partial outlines directly, avoiding an unnecessary outline rebuild and only generating missing chapters.
- Older cached completion results are invalidated and recomputed under the stronger contract after update.

## v1.0.541 — 2026-07-12

**Motion Review is optional and fully integrated.** Completion status, manual overrides, external clips, and final assembly now share one explicit contract.

- Fixed the `/episodes` status response dropping `motion_review`, which made Pipeline and Production Board show every Motion Review as pending even after whole-episode Mark Done.
- Added Motion Review to the manual per-step completion chips and labeled it optional in Pipeline, Production Board, and the Motion Review page.
- Motion Review no longer counts toward Pipeline missing-core selection, Production Board Needs Work, or Final Video prerequisites. Approved still images remain the safe default.
- Added a visible per-scene external MP4 upload in Motion Review for Chrome-extension or other third-party image-to-video results. Uploaded clips remain pending until explicitly approved with Use clip.
- Clarified assembly timing: long clips are trimmed, short clips freeze their final frame, clip audio is discarded, and every clip stays inside the scene's narration-timed window.
- Future EpisodeStatus booleans now pass through the `/episodes` response automatically, with regression tests covering Motion Review status and optional prerequisites.

## v1.0.540 — 2026-07-12

**Optional episode render workers.** Studio Hub mode can now send timestamp assemblies to a dedicated Render Studio Mac.

- Inputs are streamed through Hub, copied locally to the worker, and checksum-verified before FFmpeg starts.
- Render Studio prefers VideoToolbox, falls back to CPU encoding, fully validates the result, and retains it until Story Studio verifies the returned copy and acknowledges receipt.
- Hub grants one non-preemptive heavy-work lease per Mac, prioritizes waiting render jobs when a machine becomes free, and prefers faster M4 16 GB workers while retaining older Macs as fallbacks.
- The feature is off by default under Settings → Local Models. Unavailable workers and transition renders continue using the proven local assembler.

## v1.0.539 — 2026-07-12

**A clean two-pass visual workflow and presentation frames.** Scene timing stays stable while images and motion get separate review gates.

- **Scene Review is image-only:** generate and approve the text-to-image result without animation controls competing for attention.
- **New Motion Review:** turn approved stills into image-to-video clips, preview each result beside its source image, then choose the clip or intentionally keep the still. Replacing an image invalidates its old clip automatically.
- **One-click motion chain:** audio-paced Pipeline runs now have a durable Motion Clips step between scene rendering and final assembly. It accepts only image-to-video models, exposes provider-spend warnings, and cannot be overtaken by assembly.
- **Faster, simpler planning:** full-detail visual prompts are always on, cross-segment continuity is off by default so planning windows can run in parallel, and legacy model/window tuning is collapsed under Advanced.

- **True end-to-end runs:** Research, B-Roll selection + assembly, and timestamp assembly settings are durable preset-backed queue steps. Chain handoff failures are persisted visibly and Retry runs only unfinished work.

## v1.0.537 — 2026-07-11

**The introduction is no longer a separate tab you have to remember — it's a toggle on the Script control tab, and it can be one click.** Generating an intro used to mean switching to the Introduction tab and clicking Generate there, which was easy to forget for scripts that need one. Now:

- **"Include introduction" is a toggle on the Outline (control) tab.** It's the single switch for whether this episode has an intro — and it actually drives generation now (before, it only showed/hid a form). It's **off by default** (an intro is a per-format choice).
- **New "⚡ Generate script" button** runs the whole thing in one click: **outline → chapters → (introduction, if the toggle is on)**. It's a proper background chain, so it keeps going even if you close the page — and because the intro is chained *after* the chapters exist, it never hits the old "no script yet" problem.
- **Or keep working step-by-step:** generate the outline, review it, expand the chapters as usual — and if the toggle is on, **the introduction auto-generates the moment the chapters finish.** No tab-hop, no remembering.
- **Presets carry the toggle**, so a "Sleep Story" preset turns the intro on and a "Standard" preset leaves it off — pick a preset, get the right behaviour. The pipeline already treats the intro as an optional step, so batch runs stay consistent.

The **Introduction tab stays** — it's now just for the intro's *content* (host, length, beats, opening) and for re-rolling it. Nothing changed about how the introduction is actually written.

**Fixed: the "Scene Images" job (scenes format) now uses your whole fleet in Studio Hub mode — not just 5 at a time.** The scenes-format image generator sized its worker pool by your **image concurrency setting** (default **5**), so even in Hub mode it only ever handed the Hub 5 scenes at once — lighting up 5 studios while the rest of your fleet sat idle. In Hub mode it now scales the number of scenes it submits at once to the **number of online image studios the Hub reports** (e.g. 11), so a big render fans out across the entire fleet and finishes much faster. Direct mode is unchanged (still uses your image-concurrency setting), and chain-mode img2img renders stay serial (each scene seeds the next). ## v1.0.535 — 2026-07-10

**Studio Hub batching now covers the rest of the bulk-image jobs — scene-plan images, B-roll, and image pools.** Following [v1.0.534](#v10534--2026-07-10) (continuity render), the other multi-image jobs now also submit as ONE Hub batch in Studio Hub mode, so the Hub spreads them across your whole fleet instead of grinding one at a time:

- **Scene-plan images** ("Generate all missing" on the Scene Review page). These previously ran **one scene at a time** (each was a separate job, and the queue runs those single-image jobs serially). Now, in Hub mode with a local Image Studio model, they render as a single fleet-wide batch — a big speed-up on a long episode. Individual re-rolls are unchanged.
- **Image pools & B-roll stills** ("Generate into pool"). This was **fully serial** — one image, then the next. Now it's one batch across the fleet.

Results still stream in and are saved as each image finishes, the shared reference (for reference-driven renders) uploads once, and everything falls back to the old per-image behaviour if the Hub is unreachable or you're in Direct mode. That completes fleet-wide batching for every local bulk-image path.

## v1.0.534 — 2026-07-10

**Studio Hub: continuity render now submits a whole story as ONE batch — big renders use your entire fleet.** Previously, even in Hub mode, a continuity render fired one job per scene from a worker pool whose size came from your *direct* endpoint list — so the Hub only ever saw a handful of scenes at once and most of your Macs sat idle. Now, in Hub mode, the render **hands the Hub all its scenes in a single batch**, and the Hub work-steals them across the whole fleet (faster machines naturally doing more). On a big render (100+ scenes) that's a substantial speed-up, and it no longer depends on your direct list for parallelism. Bonus: the shared character-sheet / style reference is **uploaded once** for the whole batch, and the Hub dashboard shows a single story-level progress line. Results still stream in scene-by-scene (saved as each finishes), and if the Hub is unreachable it falls back to the per-scene path. Direct mode is unchanged.

Hit **Refresh** to see every studio on your fleet (image / voice / chat / … per Mac) with a live up/down dot, then **Restart** a stuck one, **Stop** it, or **Start** an offline one — no need to walk over to that Mac and open Pinokio. ## v1.0.528 — 2026-07-10

**New: route local generation through Studio Hub — one control-plane instead of a long list of Mac URLs. (Phase 1: chat.)** As your fleet has grown, keeping a big list of per-Mac Studio URLs in each provider's box has become fragile (it's exactly how a Voice Studio URL slipped into the image pool last release). **Settings → Local Models** now has a **Generation backend** switch:

- **Direct** — the current behaviour: Story Studio talks to each Studio Mac directly via the endpoint pools.
- **Studio Hub** — Story Studio sends the job to your Studio Hub, which delegates it to the least-busy capable Mac across the whole fleet. You configure **one** Hub URL instead of a dozen server URLs.

**Safe by design:** if the Hub is ever unreachable, generation **automatically falls back to the Direct pools** — so turning Hub mode on is low-risk, and your existing per-Studio URL lists stay in place as that fallback. When Story Studio runs on the Hub machine itself (the common case), no token is needed; a Hub token field is there only for running Story Studio from a *different* Mac. The panel shows a live Hub online/offline indicator.

This first release routes **chat / LLM** calls (idea generation, scripts, metadata, scene planning) through the Hub's gateway. **Image and voice** follow in the next updates (image reference-guided generation is waiting on a small Hub-side addition). Nothing changes unless you switch to Hub mode; Direct remains the default.

## v1.0.527 — 2026-07-10

**Fixed scene image generation failing with a cryptic "404 Not Found" — a Voice Studio server had gotten mixed into the Image Studio pool.** When generating images (e.g. Boundless EP0023), every scene could fail with `Image Studio submit failed (404): {"detail":"Not Found"}`. The cause: your Image Studio "server pool" had two **Voice Studio** modals pasted into it by mistake (they run on a different port). Voice Studio answers the same health check as Image Studio, so it looked online — but it has **no image-generation endpoint**, so every scene sent to it 404'd. Story Studio now **verifies each pooled endpoint is really Image Studio** (by the app it reports) before sending work: a mis-added Voice Studio or Chat Studio server is treated as offline and **skipped**, so scenes fail over to your real modals instead of dying. It also shows up clearly in **Settings → Local Models** now — a wrong server reads *"Not an Image Studio modal — this endpoint is Voice Studio. Remove its URL,"* instead of silently poisoning every render. (Tip: you can still tidy the list by removing those `:47870` URLs, but the app no longer breaks if you don't.)

**Fixed the Upload Plan "Apply" preview — it no longer gets cut off, and you can see every episode.** The schedule preview popover showed only the first 10 episodes (with a dead "+13 more" line you couldn't scroll to), and when the trigger button sat low on the page the whole popover ran off the bottom of the screen, hiding the Back/Apply buttons. Now it lists **all** episodes in a scrollable area, the popover is capped to the screen height (so the buttons are always reachable), and the preview is a bit wider so the scheduled dates fit on one line.

## v1.0.525 — 2026-07-09

**Fixed YouTube thumbnails silently going missing on upload — and a one-click "Backfill thumbnails" to fix the ones already uploaded.** Across your channels, **262 of 399 uploaded videos** had no thumbnail. Three separate bugs:

- **Too-large images (413).** Composed thumbnails routinely ran 2.2–2.5 MB, over YouTube's 2 MB limit, and nothing shrank them — so the upload just failed. Thumbnails are now **auto-downscaled** to under 2 MB (≤1280 px, quality stepped down as needed) before sending; small images are sent untouched.
- **Silent skip from a renamed title.** The upload resolved the thumbnail folder by the episode's *current title* instead of its *code*. If a title changed after upload, the folder wasn't found and the thumbnail step was skipped **with no error at all** — the biggest cause. It now resolves **by code** (drift-proof), the same way the rest of the app does, and never skips silently: the reason is always logged.
- **Uploaded while still processing.** The thumbnail was set the instant the upload finished, when YouTube was often still processing the video (a transient failure) with **no retry**. It now retries transient failures with backoff, and doesn't waste time retrying permanent ones (e.g. an unverified channel).

**🖼 Backfill thumbnails** button (Upload Center → Queue) sets thumbnails on already-uploaded videos that are missing one — no re-upload, just the thumbnail. It previews the exact count first (e.g. "will fix 107"), runs as a background job, is **quota-paced** (YouTube allows ~200 thumbnail sets/day, so ~225 across a channel finishes over about two days), and is **resumable** — re-run it the next day to finish. Run it per channel; it only touches videos on that channel's active account and skips episodes that have no thumbnail image on disk (make/pin one first).

## v1.0.524 — 2026-07-09

**Ideas generator remembers your last-picked LLM.** The model dropdown used to reset to OpenAI's GPT-4o every time, even after you'd chosen a different model. It now defaults to the **last model you picked** for that project — persisted per-project (in `settings/config`, alongside the other remembered Ideas-form preferences) and restored on load. If the saved model is no longer available (e.g. its API key was removed), the picker falls back to auto-selecting a usable one. A brand-new project still starts on GPT-4o until you pick something else.

## v1.0.523 — 2026-07-08

**Re-generated the audio after planning scenes? New "🎯 Reconcile timings" button re-syncs the plan to your subtitles without touching your scene images.** If you regenerate audio or re-stitch subtitles *after* a scene plan is made, the plan's timings can drift out of sync with the voice — the whole video ends up offset (we found brain-wise EP0022/EP0024 running a uniform **28 seconds ahead** of the narration, left over from an intro-skip offset the re-stitch no longer had). Re-running Scene Plan would fix the timing but generate new scenes and **forfeit every image you already made**. Reconcile timings solves it the right way: it matches each existing scene's transcript text against the *current* stitched subtitles and snaps its start/end onto the real cue times — keeping every scene id, image, and prompt. Scenes whose narration can't be found are interpolated between their neighbours and flagged for a quick look. Find it on the Scene Plan page next to Repair coverage. (Rule of thumb: **Repair coverage** fixes *gaps*; **Reconcile timings** fixes *drift* — reconcile first if the whole plan feels shifted.) EP0022 and EP0024 have already been reconciled (backups saved) — they now sit exactly on the narration, 0s uncovered, all images intact.

## v1.0.522 — 2026-07-08

**New safeguard: every second of narration must have a scene — no black screens, no frozen tails, no silently dropped audio.** Scene plans could quietly cover less audio than actually exists: the planner measured the episode by the last subtitle cue (never the real audio file), silences between chapters left 0.5–1.5s holes between scenes, and manual plan edits were never re-checked. Measured on real episodes, that meant 74s (EP0017) and **204s** (EP0018) of narration with no planned scene — which rendered as visuals drifting ahead of the voice, black/frozen tails, or the end of the narration being cut off entirely. Three layers now close this permanently:

- **Prevention at planning.** New plans are checked against the *ffprobed* merged audio before they're saved: gaps between scenes close by holding the previous scene (scene start times — the sync anchors — never move), and the final scene extends to the true audio end. A long extension is flagged loudly (⚠ "that's a long hold on one image — review or split it").
- **One-click repair for existing plans.** Scene Plan page → **🩹 Repair coverage** heals any older or hand-edited plan the same way and reports exactly what changed. (EP0017 and EP0018 have already been repaired.)
- **Hard stop at render time.** Both assemblers (Timestamps and Video Assembly in Scene Plan mode) now refuse to render when more than **2 seconds** of narration has no scene, telling you precisely where the holes are (before scene 1 / between scenes / after the last scene) and pointing at the one-click fix. Sub-2s remainders are absorbed by holding scenes to the next scene's start, so the video's length always equals the audio's. An intentional intro-skip (the sleep-story title-card hold) is still allowed on the Video Assembly path when intro/title content covers it.

## v1.0.521 — 2026-07-07

**Video Assembly now follows the Scene Plan exactly — no more rushed scenes, no more scene reuse.** On a scene-plan episode, the Video Assembly page's renderer used to treat your planned scenes as a recyclable slideshow: every scene got the uniform "seconds per scene" (default 10s) unless a fragile absolute-path match happened to recover its planned duration, crossfade overlaps silently shortened each scene, and when the images didn't fill the narration the same scenes were **repeated in a loop** — the "blows through quickly and reuses scenes" render. Now, when the scene pool is your Scene Plan renders, the render enters **plan-strict mode**: scenes play in plan order, each for exactly its planned window (`end_sec − start_sec`, matched by scene id so it works across machines and renamed folders), with recycling, shuffle, and chapter-alignment disabled and **zero scene reuse**. Crossfades anchor **on** the plan boundaries — each prepared clip carries extra tail material for the dissolve, so transitions no longer eat into any scene's time. If the narration runs past the last scene, the existing post-audio fade/hold covers the gap instead of repeating scenes. The Scene Pacing panel now explains all this in plan mode (switch the pool to Classic/Combined if you ever *want* recycled pacing); classic and image-pool/B-roll projects keep today's recycling behavior unchanged.

**Also fixed: the Timestamps assembler could wedge or flash frames on externally-made images.** Its plain no-transition path handed `.png` files whose bytes are actually JPEG (exactly what browser-extension image generators produce) to FFmpeg's extension-based decoder pick — the same wedge class as v1.0.515, which had been fixed on every path *except* this one. Such files are now detected by their real bytes and normalized once to true PNGs before the concat; genuine PNGs are untouched.

The ordering/no-reuse contract and the decoder-safe concat are now pinned by tests (`video-plan-order`, `timestamp-still-concat`, anchored-offset transition math), and the scene-plan timing contract is documented in `docs/architecture/format-contract.md`.

## v1.0.520 — 2026-07-07

**Local subtitle transcription now works whenever *any* of your Macs is online — not just the first one.** With several Voice Studio Macs configured, the "Transcribe (local)" button was disabled unless the *first-listed* Mac was reachable — even though the transcription job itself already runs on whichever Mac is free. The mismatch: the availability check the button reads only ever probed endpoint #0, while the actual job path probes the whole pool. Now the availability check probes every configured Mac in parallel and reports the feature available when **any** of them is online with the Whisper model downloaded (a model counts as ready if it's cached on any one Mac; their model lists are merged). So the first Mac can be off and you can still transcribe on the others. The same shared check gates B-roll transcription, so that's fixed too.

## v1.0.519 — 2026-07-05

**Scene-planning no longer shows "pending" when your scene images were made outside the app.** The pipeline's Scene Review status counted a scene as done only if the app *itself* had rendered its image — it read the `image_path` field the in-app renderer writes into `scene_plan.json`. Images you generate elsewhere (e.g. via a browser extension) and drop into the "05 Scene Images" folder with the correct `<scene_id>.png` name never set that field, so episodes stayed stuck at "pending" even though every image was already on disk. Status now detects scene images by **file existence** (`<scene_id>.png` in the Scene Images folder) — exactly how the Scene Review page and the video assembler already resolve them — so externally-produced images register automatically, with no manual re-link step. The new check is a strict superset of the old one, so nothing that was already complete flips back to pending. (Also repaired the two affected BrainWise episodes' plans directly, so they show complete on the current build too.)

## v1.0.518 — 2026-07-05

**One art style per project — pick it once, and every image inherits it (prompt text *and* reference image).** Image style used to leak in from four disconnected places: a style picker that was never actually applied to generation (it only rendered previews), a brand style block that was applied but wasn't a picker, and format + niche style tags merged behind the scenes. Now a project has a single **Art Style** you choose in Settings → Project. It's stored on the project and auto-applied to every image prompt for every episode, so you don't re-pick it each time — and it's still overridable per run on the Image Prompts page. When set, the project art style **replaces** the format/niche style tag rather than fighting it. If the style has a rendered preview image, that image is fed into img2img renders as a style reference so the look holds, not just the words. The new **"Whiteboard Doodle Explainer"** built-in ships in the style list (thick black marker outlines, stick figures, one idea per frame, mostly black-and-white with a few meaningful colour accents). Projects that used a brand's image style keep their look automatically — the brand style is folded in as the fallback when no art style is picked. (Note: a brand's image keywords used to *stack on top of* the format/niche look; they now define the style when no explicit art style is chosen.)

## v1.0.517 — 2026-07-05

**Subtitles now render at the size the preview shows (the 3.75× font blow-up is fixed).** Setting font size 35 in Video Assembly showed a small caption in the preview but burned in enormous text in the final video. Root cause: for static (non-animated) captions, FFmpeg interprets the subtitle style against libass's default 384×288 canvas — not the 1080p frame — so every pixel value (font size, outline, margins) got silently multiplied by 3.75 on the way to the video. (The `original_size` option the code relied on since v1.0.413 never pinned a 1080 reference; it only corrects aspect-ratio distortion.) Now every style value means the same thing everywhere: **"pixels at 1080p"**. The render path pre-scales values into the space FFmpeg actually reads (verified frame-by-frame against the bundled FFmpeg: a size-35 caption now measures identical whether burned from SRT, from an animated ASS document, or shown in the CSS preview), animated captions scale proportionally on non-1080p exports too, the preview's outline thickness now tracks the preview scale like the font does, and the "Render exact preview" cache was busted so old oversized previews don't linger. Fonts you picked while compensating for the bug will now render smaller — re-check your saved subtitle presets; what the preview shows is now what you get.

## v1.0.516 — 2026-07-05

**Fix a server hang when a route fails mid-stream (also unstuck the backend test suite).** If a route had already started sending a response and *then* threw an error, the error boundary silently swallowed it — leaving the connection open forever, so the client (the app's frontend, or a stalled download) would hang waiting for a body that never finishes. The boundary now hands these cases to Express's default handler, which closes the connection immediately so the client detects the failure instead of waiting. This same hang was what froze `npm run test:backend` at `error-boundary.test.ts` — the suite's sixth test exercised exactly this path and never completed. The test now pins the corrected behavior, and the test script also got `--test-force-exit` as a backstop so a future stray open handle can't wedge the run after all tests have finished.

## v1.0.515 — 2026-07-05

**Video Assembly "stuck at 1/160" — root cause found, reproduced, and fixed (plus renders are now dramatically faster).** Diagnosed live against the wedged EP0012 render:

- **The wedge:** nearly every scene image on disk is a **JPEG saved with a `.png` extension** (image providers return JPEG; ingest stored the bytes verbatim — this is true across all projects, going back months). The bundled **FFmpeg 8.1** picks the decoder by file extension → PNG decoder fails on the JPEG bytes → and with `-loop 1` it **retries the failed decode forever**: zero frames out, no error, no timeout. Scene 1 of 160 never finished; five animation-preview ffmpegs sat wedged for 30+ minutes the same way. Reproduced in isolation, then verified the fix: every still-image ffmpeg input now **sniffs the file's real magic bytes and pins the correct decoder** (`-c:v mjpeg`/`png`/`webp`), so all existing files render fine as-is — no data migration, no disk bloat. A file that isn't a decodable image at all now fails that scene loudly with the filename instead of hanging.
- **Speed:** three compounding fixes to scene preparation — (1) zoompan animations now feed the image **once** instead of re-decoding + re-upscaling it ~25×/second of duration; (2) the Ken Burns supersample canvas dropped from **4× (7680×4320!) to the standard 2×**, quartering zoompan's per-frame work with no visible difference (source images are ~1 MP); (3) scenes render through a **parallel pool (up to 4 at once)** instead of strictly one-by-one. Measured on the exact scene that wedged: **2.3 seconds** (was: never finishes). A 160-scene episode's prep now takes ~2 minutes.
- **Never silently stuck again:** every scene clip has a 10-minute hard ceiling (fails that scene with its number + file instead of hanging the job), progress reads "Scene clips: N/160 done" as clips complete, preview renders are capped at 2 concurrent + 90s timeout (and de-duped), so they can't pile up against a real render.
- **Scene Plan: no more runs of identical prompts.** When the single-pass planner's LLM returns an over-long scene, the salvage splitter chops it into ≤12s parts — but every part **inherited the same visual prompt verbatim** (EP0012 had scenes 95–116, twenty-two consecutive scenes, sharing one prompt → 22 near-identical images). Now only the first split part keeps the original prompt; the rest (and failed-window placeholders, which previously just sat empty behind a warning) are **auto-filled at the end of planning** with per-scene prompts generated from each part's own transcript with neighbor context.

## v1.0.514 — 2026-07-04

**Video Assembly: no more cost/duration confirmation dialog — Generate just goes.** Video assembly is a **free local ffmpeg render** (no API spend), so the cost-confirmation gate had nothing to confirm, and its duration estimate was never accurate anyway. Removed it entirely: clicking **Generate Video** now enqueues the render immediately instead of pausing on a dialog. This also eliminates the `estimate-cost` round-trip that made the dialog slow to appear. (Paid generators — scripts, images, audio, uploads — keep their confirmation, since those actually spend.)

## v1.0.513 — 2026-07-04

**Harden the SFX audio-mix on the render path (can no longer hang or look frozen).** When an episode has an enabled SFX plan, the render mixes the effects into the narration in a separate ffmpeg pass before the video render begins. Two problems: that pass ran with **no timeout** (a wedged input — e.g. a cue clip on a stalled/unplugged SSD — would hang the whole render forever with no progress), and it emitted **no status line**, so the Jobs panel sat at 0% during the mix and looked stuck. Now the mix is bounded to 10 minutes (generous — audio-only mixing is fast even on multi-hour narration; on timeout it falls back to the original un-mixed audio via the existing safety catch), and it logs `SFX: mixing N cue(s) into the audio…` before starting. Episodes **without** an SFX plan are unaffected — that path was already an instant no-op. Note: this is separate from the SFX *director* (the LLM that proposes cues), which is opt-in and button-triggered; a slow first response there is a local model loading, not the render.

## v1.0.512 — 2026-07-04

**Root-cause fix for the render crash: bound FFmpeg's stderr.** The memory watchdog added in v1.0.511 paid off immediately — the extra heap headroom kept the app alive long enough to log the real error instead of a silent abort: **`RangeError: Invalid string length` in the FFmpeg runner**. Every FFmpeg process's stderr was accumulated into one string with `stderr += chunk`, growing **unbounded** over a long render (FFmpeg prints a progress line per frame). On a long enough render it exceeded V8's maximum string length (~512 MB) — ballooning the heap to gigabytes first (the original 2026-07-04 crash) and then throwing mid-render. Fixed by capping every FFmpeg runner's buffered stderr to the **last 256 KB** (all that's needed for error diagnosis) via a shared `appendCappedTail` helper — applied to the generic runner plus the timeline, video, audio-merge, and B-roll normalize/assemble render loops. Renders of any length now hold a constant, tiny amount of log in memory. (The per-frame progress display is unaffected — it reads each chunk live, not the accumulator.)

## v1.0.511 — 2026-07-04

**Fix + diagnose the main-process crash (heap out-of-memory).** The 2026-07-04 crash was a V8 `EXC_BREAKPOINT` abort in the main process during a burst of scene-image uploads — a JavaScript **heap OOM**, which aborts V8 directly and bypasses the app's `uncaughtException` handler (so nothing was logged, and the crash report had no JS stack). The tell-tale sign was the project `/health` latency climbing 1.8s → 5s as garbage collection thrashed against a filling heap, right before the abort. Two changes: (1) the main process now runs with a **larger heap ceiling** (`--max-old-space-size`, default 4 GB, overridable via `SS_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB`) so the same workload has real headroom; (2) a **memory watchdog** logs heap/RSS every 60s (grep `mem-watch` in the `main-*.log`) and, if heap usage ever crosses 80% of the limit, writes a one-time **heap snapshot** to the logs folder — so if it ever approaches the edge again, the exact retaining objects are captured for a proper fix instead of a silent crash. Contributing factor noted for follow-up: `scene-review/upload-image` accepts base64 in a JSON body (raw body + parsed string + decoded buffer all in heap per request); moving it to raw-binary like the clip-upload endpoint would cut the per-upload footprint.

## v1.0.510 — 2026-07-04

**Video Assembly: the optional Sound/SFX step no longer gets in the way (or makes you wait on a model you didn't want).** Generating your video never uses an LLM — the render path has zero AI calls. The sound director's local model only loads when you click "🎬 Generate from narration", and what felt like "the AI model is stuck loading" was Chat Studio cold-loading that model's weights into memory on first use. Two changes so this stops surprising you:

- **The Sound/SFX section is now collapsed by default** and clearly marked skippable ("leave it closed to render with your original audio — no AI, nothing to load"). It auto-opens only when the episode already has SFX enabled or a saved plan. So the tempting primary "Generate" button (which triggers the slow local cold-load) is no longer sitting in the render flow for the common case of not wanting SFX. Click "▸ set up" only if you want it.
- **A loading expectation while directing.** When the chosen director is a local Chat Studio model, generating now shows "Loading the local model into memory — the first run can take 30–60s; later runs are fast," with a tip that a free cloud model directs almost instantly (SFX cue placement is a light task). No more mystery wait.

## v1.0.509 — 2026-07-04

### Added — fast "prompt model" for motion + thumbnail prompts (big scene-plan speedup)
Per-scene **motion prompts** and **thumbnail prompts** are short, simple LLM outputs — they don't need your strong planning/script model. But motion prompts were forced to reuse the scene-plan model, and that phase is one call *per scene* (and sequential on cloud), so it dominated long scene-plan runs.

New **"Use a separate fast model for prompts"** toggle on the Scene Plan page (motion section): pick a fast/cheap model (Haiku, a mini, or a fast local) and it's used for **motion prompts** and as the default for **thumbnail prompts**, while your planning model stays strong. Off = each step uses its own model (unchanged). Saved to project config (`prompt_model`).

Pairs with the v1.0.508 "story so far" parallel planning: Phase 1 (visual) parallelizes, Phase 2 (motion) runs on a fast model — together they cut scene-plan time substantially.

- `electron/server/generators/scene-plan.ts` (motion prompts use `prompt_model` when set), `electron/server/generators/image-prompts.ts` (thumbnail prompts fall back to `prompt_model`)
