## v1.0.508 — 2026-07-04

### Added — Scene Plan: “Story so far” continuity toggle → parallel segment planning (much faster)
The scene planner splits long episodes into time-segments and, until now, **always** planned them **sequentially** — because each segment carried a rolling *"story so far"* recap of earlier segments for cross-seam visual continuity. That recap is exactly what forced the sequence, and it's the main reason a long video's plan takes so long.

There's now a **“Story so far” continuity** toggle on the Scene Plan page (single-pass mode):
- **On (default)** — unchanged: segments plan one-after-another with the rolling recap, so recurring characters/setting/tone carry across seams.
- **Off** — segments are planned **in parallel** (each purely from its own cues + fixed time bounds), a large speedup on multi-segment episodes. The trade-off is weaker continuity *across* segment seams (within a segment is unchanged).

Parallelism is model-gated for safety: **direct paid cloud models fan out** (4× by default); a local Chat Studio pool uses its endpoints; free/proxy tiers stay serial (parallel there would just multiply 429s). The setting **saves into scene-plan presets** (along with motion-prompt + window-size toggles), so you can keep a "fast" preset and a "max-continuity" preset.

Progress now reads *"Story-so-far OFF — planning 8 segments 4× in parallel"* when enabled.

### Files
- `electron/server/models/types.ts` (`cross_window_context`), `electron/server/services/scene-planner.ts` (parallel vs chained window planning), `electron/server/generators/scene-plan.ts` + `electron/server/routes/scene-plan.ts` (thread the flag)
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/scene-plan.vue` (toggle + preset persistence)

## v1.0.507 — 2026-07-04

### Fixed — Scene Plan: motion prompts now get the same crash protection as image prompts
The scene planner writes image (visual) prompts in time-chunked segments, but the whole plan was only saved to disk **once, after** the motion-prompt phase — so if motion generation crashed, was cancelled, or the app restarted, the (expensive) **image scenes were lost too**. Now:
- The plan is **saved right after the visual-prompt phase**, before motion generation starts — so image scenes always survive.
- **Motion prompts save incrementally** (every ~10 scenes) during their phase, so finished ones survive a mid-phase interruption too.
- **Phase-specific progress**: the log now reads *"Planned segment 5/8 — 122 image scene(s) so far…"* during planning, then *"120/122 motion prompt(s) so far…"* during the motion phase, so you can see which phase is running.

### Fixed — kie.ai audio recovers for free on re-run (retry-then-repair)
Re-running Generate already auto-recovers completed-but-lost work for free before paying to regenerate — but this was wired for GenAIPro/fal audio and kie **images**, not kie **audio**. So re-running a kie-audio episode would *regenerate* (re-charge) instead of recovering. **kie audio is now in the recover-before-regenerate path**, so re-running an episode skips what's present, free-recovers completed kie chunks, and only re-pays for the genuinely-missing.

### Added — Jobs tab: status filter, "Repair all failed", and per-card repair result
- **Status filter** — new chips (All · Running · Queued · Failed · Done · Cancelled, with counts) to show just the jobs you care about. Complements the existing type tabs + sort.
- **🔧 Repair all failed (N)** — one button that repairs *every* failed/cancelled job that can be repaired (free — polls each provider + downloads, never re-submits). The true "recover everything the providers already finished" action. Previously the bulk button only covered app-restart-interrupted jobs.
- **Per-card repair result** — Repair used to only flash a toast, so the card stayed red and you couldn't tell which you'd clicked. Each card now shows a persistent chip (`✓ recovered 3 — all present`, `0 recovered, 8 left — Retry`, etc.).

### Fixed — Repair reconciler messaging is provider-aware
A kie/fal episode's Repair no longer misleadingly logs *"Text-matching against GenAIPro history"* — the GenAIPro-only fallback runs only for GenAIPro episodes; others get a clear provider-appropriate "regenerate" note.

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/scene-plan.ts` (pre-motion save + incremental motion save + phase progress)
- `electron/server/lib/manifest-recovery.ts`, `electron/server/generators/audio.ts` (kie audio retry-then-repair)
- `electron/server/services/audio-reconciler.ts` (provider-aware fallback messaging)
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/jobs.vue` (status filter, Repair-all-failed, per-card chip)

## v1.0.506 — 2026-07-04

### Fixed — kie.ai audio: transient "fetch failed" no longer kills 1–2 chunks per batch
The kie.ai TTS client had **no retry** (unlike every other provider), so a single transient network blip — a dropped/reset connection under concurrent batch load — on *any* of a chunk's requests failed the whole chunk. That's why batch audio kept losing 1–2 random chapters per episode with "fetch failed" on `kie-eleven-turbo-v2.5`.

Now the kie client is resilient, matching the other providers:
- **Submit** (`createTask`) retries up to 4× on network errors / 429 / 5xx with exponential backoff (honoring `Retry-After`). Only retried on a *thrown* fetch (no response), so it won't double-charge.
- **Poll** (`recordInfo`) no longer dies on a transient error — it backs off and keeps polling (the task is still running on kie's side), giving up only after 6 consecutive failures.
- **Download** of the finished audio URL retries up to 3× (re-fetching the same URL is free, no re-charge).

Net effect: occasional kie hiccups are absorbed instead of failing chunks. If kie is genuinely rate-limiting, the backoff respects it. Re-run any affected episodes (Skip existing remakes only the missing chapters).

### Files
- `electron/server/lib/kie-tts-client.ts` (retry + backoff on submit/poll), `electron/server/generators/audio.ts` (download retry in the kie branch)

---

## v1.0.505 — 2026-07-04

### Improved — clearer error when an OpenAI image model blocks a prompt
kie.ai relays OpenAI GPT-Image / DALL·E content-policy rejections as a bare `state:fail` with **no reason**, so a blocked thumbnail/scene prompt used to fail with the unhelpful "kie.ai reported a failed task with no error message." Now, when the failing model is a GPT-Image / GPT-4o / DALL·E model and kie returned no reason, the error says so plainly and points you at the fix:

> *Image generation blocked — gpt-image-2 returned no reason, which almost always means OpenAI's content policy rejected the prompt (graphic violence, gore, open wounds, injury, etc.). Soften the prompt, or switch this step to a less-restrictive image model (e.g. Flux, Seedream, or nano-banana).*

Also reads a couple more kie error fields (`failMsg`, `failReason`) before falling back, and applies the same hint to the image repair-by-task path.

### Also — Jobs-tab audio Repair confirmed provider-aware
The per-job **Repair** button on an audio job (Jobs page) calls the same `/audio-repair` route that became provider-aware in v1.0.504, so it now recovers **kie.ai and fal.ai** chunks (from the task-manifest sidecar), not just GenAIPro. Removed a stale `provider: 'genaipro'` hint from the request (the route ignores it now).

## v1.0.504 — 2026-07-03

### Fixed — Audio "Repair missing" now works for kie.ai and fal.ai (not just GenAIPro)
The Audio-integrity **Repair missing** recovery was hard-wired to GenAIPro — it rejected every other provider ("only GenAIPro can reconcile"), so a kie.ai (or fal.ai) job that completed on the provider but lost the download couldn't be recovered. Repair is now **provider-aware**:

- **kie.ai** — the kie taskId is now recorded when each chunk is submitted, and Repair re-fetches the finished audio from kie's task history (`recordInfo`). *(Only losses from this version on are recoverable — older kie chunks recorded no taskId.)*
- **fal.ai** — Repair re-polls the stored fal status/result URLs (fal already recorded them; the reconciler just wasn't using them).
- **GenAIPro** — unchanged, including the text-match fallback across its 1-day history.
- **Streaming providers** (direct ElevenLabs, Fish Audio, Voice Studio, macOS) have **no server-side task** to re-fetch — Repair now says so plainly and points you to **Regenerate** (Skip existing remakes only the missing chunk).

The reconciler resolves each provider's key the same way the generator does (accounts + app-secrets). The panel copy is generalized from "GenAIPro" to "the provider".

### Files
- `electron/server/services/audio-reconciler.ts` (provider-aware `reconcileAudio`; per-provider re-fetch dispatch; GenAIPro text-match kept)
- `electron/server/lib/kie-tts-client.ts` (`onTaskSubmitted` + `fetchKieAudioUrlByTaskId`), `electron/server/generators/audio.ts` (record kie taskId on submit)

The Audio Generator can now route ElevenLabs voices through **kie.ai** — a fourth gateway alongside direct / fal / GenAIPro, and the **cheapest per character**. Three models appear in the audio model picker (Cloud paid), using the same ElevenLabs voice ids you already use:

- **ElevenLabs Multilingual v2 [kie.ai]** — $0.06 / 1k chars

Under the hood it's kie's unified jobs API (createTask → poll → download the finished audio), mirroring the existing kie image client and the genaipro/fal audio path. v3 uses kie's text-to-dialogue endpoint as a single narration turn. Voice previews work too.

## v1.0.502 — 2026-07-03

**Fix: "No tokens for this account" after reconnecting YouTube.** Disconnecting and reconnecting the SAME channel minted a fresh internal account id (the disconnect wiped the record before the reconnect could match it), which orphaned every schedule plan and episode sidecar still pointing at the old id — so every reschedule failed with "No tokens for this account — reconnect YouTube" even though the account was freshly connected. Three-part fix: (1) reconnecting the same channel now **reuses the previous account id** (disconnect stashes the removed account's identity; a different channel still gets a fresh id); (2) plan apply and the per-row schedule/unschedule now **self-heal stale bindings** — when the stored account id is orphaned, they resolve to the project's current (single) account, persist the fix back to the plan and sidecars, and proceed; (3) since projects are single-account by design, this can never route to a wrong channel — an account that still exists but lost its tokens keeps the explicit "reconnect" error. Your stuck episodes fix themselves on the next Apply / Retry.

## v1.0.501 — 2026-07-03

**Upload Center: a persistent operation report + one clear banner for expired YouTube sessions.** The two highest-impact trust fixes from the Upload Center review:

- **Operation report card.** Applying a plan (or Apply + Upload) now leaves a persistent per-episode receipt below the tabs — every episode with what happened (`Scheduled on YouTube`, `Scheduled locally`, `Scheduled + upload queued`, `Skipped — already public / no final video`) and, for failures, the **actual reason** plus a per-row **Retry** button (retries the YouTube schedule update or the upload for just that episode). Failures sort to the top with a "N need attention" chip. Toasts remain as the one-line summary; the card is the detailed record that doesn't vanish after 5 seconds.
- **"YouTube session expired" banner.** When Google expires or revokes an account's token (`invalid_grant`), every panel on the page (playlists, orphans, sync, statuses) used to fail independently with six identical raw-stack error toasts. The backend now tags this error class (`code: youtube_auth_expired`, friendly message + hint), and the Upload page collapses all of them into **one** banner: what happened, how to fix it (Accounts → Disconnect → Connect), an "Open Accounts" shortcut, and an "I've reconnected — retry" button that reloads the affected panels. The silent auto-sync also raises the banner instead of failing invisibly.

## v1.0.500 — 2026-07-03

**Upload Center: schedule errors now say WHY, slots follow episode order, and the queue stops defaulting to old uploaded rows.** Three fixes from the capi session:

- **No more silent "patch failure(s)".** When applying a plan, YouTube's per-video update failures were counted but their reasons thrown away — you saw "2 patch failure(s)" with no clue why. The apply toasts now include the actual reasons per episode (e.g. `CAPI0003: The video is already public — publishAt rejected`), partial failures surface as an error toast instead of a green success, and the per-row schedule popover shows a failed YouTube update as an error (with the reason) rather than a green "saved" with the failure buried in parentheses. Every catch also falls back to the underlying message instead of a bare "Apply failed".
- **Schedule slots now map onto episode order.** Slots were assigned in the order episodes were selected/uploaded, so a later episode uploaded first grabbed the earlier publish slot. Both the scope picker and the backend apply endpoint now sort the batch by episode code (numeric-aware, EP2 < EP10) before pairing with consecutive slots — earliest episode always publishes first, regardless of click or upload order.
- **Queue stops re-adding old uploaded rows on every visit.** The 🪦 "Deleted upstream" chip auto-activates when takedowns exist — but its dismissal only lasted the session, so every page visit re-merged years-old uploaded-then-deleted rows into the default "Ready" view, sorted oldest-first on top. Dismissing the chip is now remembered per project (keyed by the tombstone set, so a NEW takedown still auto-surfaces). The default view is back to what it says: ready-to-upload episodes only.

## v1.0.499 — 2026-07-02

**Scene planner: the art style now leads the prompt, so weaker image models actually apply it.** Previously the global visual style was handed to the prompt-writing LLM with a "weave it in naturally" instruction — which smaller / local models often ignored or buried at the end of the description, where image models under-weight it (leading tokens carry far more weight than trailing ones). Now the exact style clause is placed deterministically at the **front** of every scene's `visual_prompt` (e.g. *"Soft watercolor illustration. A deer stands in a misty forest…"*), regardless of what the model does. The planner is told the style is context-only and not to restate it, so scene content still suits the style without duplicating it; if a prompt already opens with the style it isn't doubled. Applies to both the two-pass planner (and "Regen empty prompts" / per-scene re-plan) and the single-pass windowed planner. Existing plans are unchanged — re-plan or regen a scene to apply the new ordering.

## v1.0.498 — 2026-07-02

**Model picker: Local / Cloud·free / Cloud·paid tabs so you can't spend by accident.** Every LLM model now carries a cost tier, and the AI-model dropdown shows filter tabs — **All · Local · Cloud · free · Cloud · paid** (with counts) — that narrow the list to just that tier. Pick "Cloud · free" and no paid model can be selected; the tabs appear only when your list actually spans more than one tier (i.e. once Chat Studio is configured). Paid models are also flagged inline with a **💲 paid** marker and a tooltip ("uses your credits") in the "All" view, so an accidental click stands out even without switching tabs. Tiers: local Chat Studio MLX models → **Local**; Chat Studio's free cloud providers (NVIDIA NIM, Groq, Gemini free, HF Router, …) → **Cloud · free**; anything that spends credits (OpenAI, DeepSeek, OpenRouter-direct, and Chat Studio's paid providers like Anthropic / OpenAI / xAI / Together) → **Cloud · paid**. Applies everywhere the model picker appears (Scene Plan, Scene Review, Co-writer, Scripts, Ideas, Research, Metadata, …). The tier is read from Chat Studio's per-model `free` flag, so it stays accurate as you add providers on that side.

## v1.0.497 — 2026-07-02

**Scene planner: the mystery "502 (no body)" is fixed — and Chat Studio's new free cloud providers get their own picker group.** Three related changes after diagnosing the two-pass run that finished with only pacing:

- **Real error messages instead of "502 status code (no body)".** Chat Studio returns errors as `{"detail": "…"}` (FastAPI style), which the OpenAI SDK can't parse — so the actual diagnostic ("OpenRouter returned HTTP 429: model is temporarily rate-limited upstream, retry shortly") was swallowed and every failure looked like a dead server. The provider now extracts the detail and surfaces it verbatim. What actually happened to your run: the free-tier cloud model was **rate-limited upstream**, pass 1 (deterministic pacing split) needs no LLM so it succeeded, and pass 2's per-scene calls all failed.
- **Rate-limit-aware retries.** A rate-limited free tier now backs off 15–45s between attempts instead of hammering it every 1.2s (which just extends the limit window), and Chat Studio **cloud-proxied** models stay sequential even with multiple endpoints configured — every endpoint proxies the same upstream, so fanning out only multiplies 429s. A rate-limit error also no longer marks the (healthy) endpoint as down. Tip: after a partial run, use **"✨ Regen N empty prompts only"** — it keeps the pacing and fills just the missing prompts.
- **Cloud/local split for Chat Studio models.** Chat Studio ≥1.15 proxies free cloud LLM providers (OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, Groq, Cerebras, Gemini, Hugging Face Router, SambaNova, GitHub Models) and its raw model list ballooned to ~450 entries flooding the picker. Story Studio now reads Chat Studio's curated `/api/providers` catalog instead: local MLX models stay under **"Chat Studio (local)"**, and the curated free cloud models appear under a new **"Chat Studio (cloud · free APIs)"** group (~74 entries, each labeled with its provider). Providers whose API key isn't configured in Chat Studio show disabled with an "add key in Chat Studio" note. Old Chat Studio builds without the catalog endpoint keep the previous behaviour (locals only).

## v1.0.496 — 2026-07-01

**Preview the stitched timeline subtitles too.** Building on the per-chapter cue preview (v1.0.494), the "Stitch into the timeline" section now has a **👁 Preview stitched** button that shows the unified `<code>_stitched.srt` — the exact file Scene Plan reads and Video Assembly burns in — with every cue's timestamp and text on the global timeline. The preview panel is now a shared component (`SubtitleCuePreview`) rendered next to whichever button opened it, so per-chapter files preview in the file list and the stitched file previews in the stitch section.

## v1.0.495 — 2026-07-01

**Fix: Chrome extensions couldn't reach the server-mode API from another machine (Private Network Access).** The `story-studio-tts` and `story-studio-bulk-asset` extensions worked from `localhost` but failed with a generic `TypeError: Failed to fetch` when the browser ran on a different machine than Story Studio KH (e.g. an iMac reaching this Mac mini over Tailscale) — even though the server was reachable and host permissions were granted. Chrome's Private Network Access policy blocks such fetches before they leave the browser unless the server answers the CORS preflight with `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true`, which the `cors` package doesn't send. Added a tiny middleware (server mode only) that sets that header when the preflight requests private-network access. `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` are exempt from PNA, so desktop-loopback mode was never affected and is unchanged.

## v1.0.494 — 2026-07-01

**Preview generated subtitles in the Subtitles tab.** Each file in the "Subtitle files" list now has a 👁 button that opens an inline preview of the actual cues — every line's timestamp (`start → end`) and text — so you can verify transcription accuracy without opening Finder or a text editor. Click the eye again (or ✕) to close; the panel header shows the cue count and total duration. Deleting the previewed file or switching episodes closes it automatically. Backed by a new read endpoint that parses the `.srt`/`.vtt` cues (`.ass` files show their raw text), with the same strict filename validation as delete (no path traversal, subtitle extensions only) and a 2000-cue cap on the response.

## v1.0.493 — 2026-07-01

**Fix: Chat Studio (local LLM) no longer keeps hammering an offline server, and its Settings status stays fresh.** Two issues fixed:

- **Repeated hangs on an offline endpoint.** Every generation attempt ran a fresh ~4-second reachability probe before dispatching. A single-endpoint setup has no pool "down-state" to lean on, so a batch run (scene plan, ideas, cowriter) re-paid that 4s on *every* call against a powered-down Chat Studio. There's now a short-lived **health cache** — a just-failed endpoint is remembered as offline for ~12s (and a healthy one trusted for ~5s), so repeated attempts short-circuit instantly instead of stacking up timeouts. A live request that dies mid-call marks its endpoint offline too, and a fresh long run (e.g. a new scene-plan job) clears the cache so a recovered server is re-probed immediately.
- **Stale online/offline dot in Settings → Local Models.** The ●/○ indicator only updated when you manually clicked "Test", so it drifted out of sync after the server was started/stopped. It now **auto-refreshes every 30 seconds** (quietly, enabled endpoints only) for all local Studios (Chat / Image / Voice), so what you see matches reality.

Note: this is a Story-Studio-side fix — Chat Studio being offline is normal; the app just handles it far better now.

It now uses the same `.create-modal` card styling as every other modal (solid background, border, padding, shadow).

Because each button refused to shrink below its text, the row overflowed the rail and the **SFX** tab spilled rightward underneath the selected pool's title ("Prayer B-roll" etc.), making it unclickable. The filters are now a contained 2×2 grid that always stays within the rail.

## v1.0.490 — 2026-06-30

### Added — Scripted B-Roll Phase 4: styled AI-gen fallback
For beats that **no stock clip** covers, Scripted B-Roll can now **generate a channel-styled clip** instead of leaving them empty. Tick **"AI-generate clips for beats with no stock match"**, set a **channel style** (e.g. "flat editorial illustration", "muted 2D vector") and pick an **image model** — then during Resolve, every still-empty beat gets a styled still (subject prefixed with your style), converted to a 1080p clip and dropped into the **same video pool**, so it concatenates seamlessly with the stock footage. No separate render path.

- Reuses your project's existing image-generation stack (same providers/keys as the Image Pool generator). The style prefix keeps fallbacks visually consistent and clearly stylised — they read as "our channel's b-roll", never as fake real footage.
- Stock-first: AI-gen only runs for beats stock couldn't fill, and only when you opt in (it costs image credits). Works even with no Pexels/Pixabay key (pure AI-gen mode).
- Best-effort: a generation or conversion failure just leaves that beat empty; it never breaks Resolve.

This completes the Scripted B-Roll sourcing chain (stock → AI-gen) from the spec. Extra paid providers (Storyblocks) + a logo side-channel remain optional follow-ups.

## v1.0.487 — 2026-06-30

### Added — Scripted B-Roll (beta): narration → targeted stock footage
A new **Scripted B-Roll** section in Video Assembly (Step 1) builds a video where each line of narration is illustrated by a *matching* stock clip, instead of random pool footage. An LLM **shot director** reads the episode's stitched subtitles, splits them into timed beats, and writes **filmable search queries** per beat (the craft: "economic uncertainty" → "stock market ticker red", "worried trader at desk"). Each beat's clip is then pulled from **Pexels/Pixabay** into your B-Roll pool and lined up to the narration timing.

- **Generate shot plan** — pick a director model, beat length, and optional style hint; get a per-beat plan (line + queries). Tick "Download clips now" to immediately search + fetch a clip for every beat.
- **Download / re-match** — searches each beat's queries across Pexels/Pixabay, downloads the pick into your video pool (provenance + index, no-repeat across beats), and records it on the beat. Clips compound in the pool just like SFX.
- **Assemble** — bridges the resolved plan to the existing B-Roll selection sidecar and queues the **existing** assembler, so beats render in order at their narration timing (stock-clip audio muted; narration + the SFX layer own the sound). The **universal SFX sound layer rides on top for free.**

Safe + additive: the plan is its own `broll_plan.json` sidecar with an opt-in gate; the existing "load random clips" path and every other format are untouched. This is **Phase 1** — storyboard swap/regenerate UI, the styled AI-gen fallback for beats stock can't cover, and extra providers (Storyblocks / logos) are queued (see `docs/scripted-broll-format-spec.md`).

### Files

- `electron/server/routes/broll-shots.ts` (+ `routes/index.ts`) — get/save/delete/generate/resolve/assemble

## v1.0.486 — 2026-06-30

### Added — SFX auto-fetch from Freesound (seeds your sound pool)
The Sound / SFX layer can now **fill the cues your pools don't cover by downloading them from Freesound** — straight into your SFX pool, tagged and ready to reuse. Turn on **"Auto-fetch missing effects from Freesound"** in the Sound section; when you Generate (or hit "Re-match + fetch"), any unmatched bed/spot is searched on Freesound, the best preview is downloaded into your audio pool, given provenance + tags, and matched to the cue.

This is what **bootstraps the library**: the first few videos fetch a lot, but every fetch lands permanently in the pool, so later videos increasingly match locally (instant + free) and only reach out for genuinely novel sounds. The pool is a compounding asset.

- Reuses the existing Freesound adapter + provenance + indexer (same path as manual B-Roll Fetch). Downloads target the first online SFX (audio) pool, or a specific one via `fetch_pool_id`.
- Already-fetched sounds are de-duplicated by Freesound id, never re-downloaded. Spot one-shots stay no-repeat within an episode.
- Best-effort + safe: no Freesound key, no audio pool, or any network error just leaves the cue empty (a clear note is surfaced) — it never blocks generation or the render.

Auto-generate with ElevenLabs for cues even Freesound can't cover remains a queued follow-up.

## v1.0.485 — 2026-06-29

### Added — Sound / SFX layer in Video Assembly (universal, all formats)
A new **Sound / SFX** section in Video Assembly (Step 5, under Subtitles) adds sound effects to any narrated video, regardless of format. An LLM **sound director** reads the episode's stitched **subtitle timing** and proposes a *sparse* set of cues — **ambient beds** (atmosphere over a span) and **spot one-shots** (a sound at a moment) — which are matched to clips from your **SFX pools** (the v1.0.481 audio pools) and mixed under the narration at render time.

- **Generate from narration** — pick a director model + density (minimal / moderate / rich) and the LLM proposes beds + spots from the timed transcript. Needs the episode's stitched subtitles (run the Subtitles step first).
- **Review + edit** — each cue is a row: label, timing, gain, the matched clip (swap to any pool clip), mute, or remove. Add beds/spots manually too. "Re-match to pools" re-runs matching after you add clips; spots are no-repeat.
- **Safe + reversible** — the whole feature is opt-in via a master toggle. With no plan, the toggle off, or no cue resolved to a clip, the video renders **exactly as before**. The mixer writes a *new* audio file consumed through the renderer's existing merged-audio path, so the core composition is untouched; any mix failure falls back to the original audio.

Resolution is **SFX-pool only** for now; auto-fetch from Freesound / auto-generate with ElevenLabs for unmatched cues, visual-driven cues, and a Freesound credits roll-up are the queued follow-ups (see `docs/sfx-sound-layer-spec.md`).

- `electron/server/services/sfx-director.ts` (subtitle→cues LLM: prompt, tolerant parse, unresolved-plan mapping), `electron/server/services/sfx-resolver.ts` (label↔tag matcher, no-repeat, pool adapters, plan→mix cues)

## v1.0.484 — 2026-06-29

### Added — Characters: one app-level library, assignable per project
The two character systems are being unified into **one app-level library** where each character can be **assigned (tagged) to one or more projects** — instead of the old split between per-project characters and snapshot-only library copies. A project's **Characters** page is now a filtered view: it shows the project's own characters **plus** every library character assigned to it, and a new **"📚 Assign from library"** button lets you attach an existing library character to the project. Library-assigned rows show a **From library** badge and an **Unassign** action (which leaves the library entry untouched). The **Character Library** page now shows how many projects each character is assigned to.

This ships **safely and non-destructively** — nothing is deleted or rewritten:
- The change is **additive**: a new optional `projects: string[]` tag set on the library record records assignments. Records without it behave exactly as before.
- The unification happens at the **read layer** — `character-manager`'s `listCharacters` / `getCharacter` / `resolveCharacters` / `referenceImagePath` now merge in assigned library characters (deduped by id, the on-disk project copy winning), so **every consumer** (script gen, image gen, image-prompts, audio/voice routing, continuity render, the picker) sees the unified view with no per-consumer change.
- A one-time consolidation migration is provided **copy-only, dry-run-by-default, verified, and reversible** — `GET /api/character-migration/plan` (dry run, writes nothing) and `POST /api/character-migration/run` (requires `{ confirm: true }`). It copies per-project characters into the library tagged with their slug, verifies each copy, **never deletes the originals**, and skips id conflicts rather than overwriting.

See `docs/character-unification-spec.md` for the full design, safety contract, and rollback.

- `electron/server/models/types.ts` (`Character.projects?: string[]`; `source` gains `'library'`)
- `electron/server/services/character-library.ts` (`assignToProject` / `unassignFromProject` / `setProjects` / `listForProject` / `libraryCharacterDir`; `saveToLibrary` auto-assigns source project; `projects` preserved on update; dropped on snapshot import)
- `electron/server/services/character-manager.ts` (`listOwnCharacters` project-only vs unified `listCharacters`; `getCharacter` + `referenceImagePath` library fallback)

## v1.0.481 — 2026-06-29

### Added — SFX pools get fetch (Freesound) + generate (ElevenLabs)
Audio (SFX) pools can now be **filled without leaving the app**, mirroring the B-Roll Fetch flow:

The Fetch panel now **gates providers by pool media**: SFX pools see Freesound + Generate; video pools see Pexels / Pixabay / NASA. You can't accidentally drop video into an audio pool (or vice-versa) — the search route rejects a media mismatch.

The app-level pool library now holds **three media types** — B-Roll video, still images, and **sound effects (SFX)** — so it's been renamed **Assets Library** (sidebar + page). ## v1.0.478 — 2026-06-29

**Per-model aspect ratios + quality tiers from Image Studio's size menu.** When a selected Image Studio model advertises its own `sizes` menu (new `/imagestudio/models` contract), the **Aspect Ratio** list now comes from that model's real options, and a new **Quality** control (Highest / Balanced / Fast) replaces the old local-only Render Size scale. Quality resolves per model against the menu — **Highest** = the largest size offered for the chosen aspect (`ultra` → `high` → max), **Balanced** = a sensible mid size (e.g. ~1080p for 16:9), **Fast** = the smallest — so a saved preset (aspect + tier) stays usable across different models and suppliers. This also lifts the old local-resolution cap for **cloud** models: a cloud model with a size menu now sends its full higher-res dimensions instead of being limited to the local preset table. Switching to a model that doesn't offer your current aspect snaps it to that model's default aspect so the picker is never blank. **Backward-compatible:** models with no `sizes` menu (kie cloud models, older Image Studio builds) keep the previous behaviour exactly — local models show the Render Size scale, cloud models use the aspect string — so this activates automatically once your Image Studio fleet is updated to serve the new fields.

## v1.0.477 — 2026-06-28

**Honor Image Studio's "needs API key" signal for cloud models.** A cloud model whose required credential isn't configured (Cloudflare / Together) is now shown as **"needs key"** and is unselectable, instead of appearing ready and failing at generate time. Story Studio reads this **defensively** — a cloud model is treated as not-ready if Image Studio reports either `cloud_credentials_ok: false` **or** `fit.state: "needs_key"`. Pollinations (no key required) stays always-available. Backward-compatible: on an Image Studio build that doesn't send either signal yet, cloud models behave as before (ready) — so this quietly activates once you update Image Studio.

## v1.0.476 — 2026-06-28

**Image Studio cloud models are now selectable, and the picker is decluttered.**
- **Cloud models work now** (Flux Schnell via Together AI / Cloudflare / Pollinations). Image Studio was exposing them all along; Story Studio was wrongly marking them unavailable because it derived "ready" from the *local-engine* diagnostics, which don't cover cloud-proxied models. They're now treated as always-ready (no local engine / download / memory needed) and selectable, tagged with their cloud provider.
- **The list only shows models you can actually use.** Instead of dumping Image Studio's entire catalog (most of which isn't downloaded), the picker now shows **cloud models + locally downloaded models only** — the not-yet-downloaded long tail is hidden. (Falls back to the old behavior on older Image Studio builds that don't report download state.)

## v1.0.475 — 2026-06-28

**UI for the image-to-video / animation settings (no more config-file editing).**
- **Scene Plan** now has motion controls: a **"Generate motion prompts"** toggle and a **Motion level (1–4)** picker (persist to project config — `motion_prompts_enabled` / `default_motion_level`, previously settable only via the API).
- **Scene Review** now has a **"≥ sec" minimum-animation-length** field next to the Animate model picker (`animate_min_seconds`). Bulk "Animate missing" only animates scenes that are approved, have a motion prompt, and are at least this long — short beats stay stills. Its tooltip now spells out that gating, so skipped scenes aren't a mystery.

## v1.0.474 — 2026-06-28

**Animation gating — approve first, and only animate scenes worth animating.** Bulk clip generation ("render missing clips") now skips a scene unless it's **approved** AND has a **motion prompt** AND its window is **≥ `animate_min_seconds`** (a new per-project setting, default 0 = no floor). This means you never spend a clip on an image you haven't greenlit, and short beats (e.g. 2–3s) stay stills instead of being needlessly animated — set `animate_min_seconds` (e.g. 4) per project to tune how much gets animated. Clearing a scene's motion prompt remains the per-scene "don't animate this one" override. The `GET …/scene-review/:episodeId` response now also returns `animate_min_seconds` so external animators (the Chrome i2v extension) apply the exact same rule. Single per-scene "generate clip" stays a deliberate, ungated action.

## v1.0.473 — 2026-06-28

**Ingest externally-generated clips (and images) into the planned scenes.** You can now build scene images *and* animated clips outside the app (e.g. a Chrome-extension image→motion-prompt→video flow) and feed them straight into the scene plan — fully interchangeable with the in-app fal/kie generators.

- **New: `POST /projects/:slug/scene-review/:episodeId/upload-clip/:sceneId`** — saves a raw-binary mp4 (Content-Type `video/mp4`, route-scoped 256 MB cap since the app-wide JSON limit is 10 MB) to `11 Video Assets/<scene-id>.mp4` — the exact location + filename the in-app clip generator writes and the final-video assembler scans for. It validates the scene id (path-traversal-safe), checks the scene exists in `scene_plan.json`, sniffs for a real mp4, writes atomically (tmp→rename so the assembler never reads a half-written file), and stamps `clip_path` + `rendered_motion_prompt`. Because the assembler detects a clip by **file existence** keyed to the scene id, an ingested clip drops into the final video at exactly the planned scene's position/timing — same as a fal/kie clip.
- **Image ingest** (existing `upload-image/:sceneId`) now also stamps `rendered_prompt`, so an externally-ingested image isn't mis-flagged as stale in Scene Review.
- Both sources coexist safely: generate via fal/kie **or** ingest externally, per scene, with no conflict.

## v1.0.472 — 2026-06-28

**Search the AI-model picker.** The LLM model selector now has a search box — type part of a model's name or provider (e.g. "opus", "gemini", "chat studio") to filter the dropdown instead of scrolling every provider's full list. It appears once a project has more than a handful of models, matches across name / id / provider, and always keeps your current selection in the list so the picker never goes blank while filtering. Applies everywhere LLM selection happens (Scene Plan, Scene Review, Scripts, Co-writer, Ideas, Metadata, Research, Image Prompts, and more — they all share the one selector).

## v1.0.471 — 2026-06-28

**Animated clips now flow into the final video — Phase 3.** The timestamp video assembler now uses a scene's animated clip (from "11 Video Assets") instead of its still whenever one exists, completing the image → motion-prompt → clip → final-video pipeline.

- When **any** scene has a clip, each scene is normalised to a uniform chunk at the export resolution/fps, exactly its window long: a **still is looped** (unchanged behaviour), a **clip is scaled/padded then fit to the window** — its last frame freezes to fill a short clip, and the tail trims for a long one. Clip audio is dropped (narration stays the audio track). Chunks are then concatenated.
- **Still-only episodes are completely unaffected** — they keep the existing fast concat-of-stills path, so there's zero change (or perf cost) unless you've actually animated scenes.
- Subtitles burn-in and music/ambient beds work the same in clips mode. **Transitions (crossfade etc.) are skipped when clips are present** (scenes hard-cut) — blending real motion clips is left for a future pass; the assembler logs this clearly.

## v1.0.458 — 2026-06-23

**Bulk "Regen N prompts only" now fans out across your whole LM Studio pool — and transient disconnects retry instead of leaving prompts blank.** Two fixes to scene-plan prompt regeneration:

- **Parallel bulk regen.** The "✨ Regen N prompts only" button used to fire **one job per scene and wait for each before queuing the next** — so reprompting 47 empty scenes pushed them serially through a single endpoint, leaving the rest of your model pool idle and taking far longer than it should. It now submits a **single job** that regenerates every empty prompt **in parallel across all configured LM Studio endpoints** (one scene per endpoint, chunked at pool size), exactly like the two-pass planner's prompt pass. On a 3-endpoint setup that's roughly 3× faster. Cancel now stops the backend job (it polls between chunks), not just the frontend loop.
- **Retry on transient failures.** When a local model briefly drops the connection mid-generation, that scene's prompt used to be left **permanently empty** for you to reprompt by hand. Per-scene generation now **retries up to 3 attempts** (short backoff, re-picking a pool endpoint each time) before giving up — so a momentary disconnect self-heals instead of leaving a hole. This applies to both the initial two-pass plan and the bulk regen.

Shared one code path (`generatePromptsForScenes`) so the initial plan and the bulk regen behave identically. Prompts that already exist are kept and used as continuity context; time ranges and transcripts are never touched.

## v1.0.457 — 2026-06-22

**Unified scene-image storage — Phase 1.** Continuity / Scene Review renders used to save into a separate flat `scene_images/` folder at the episode root, while the Scene Generator saved into the named "{code} - NN Scene Images" folder — two locations, bad UX, and the flat one got **left behind in iCloud** when media migrated to an external root (it wasn't in the migrated folder set). Now **both paths write into the named "NN Scene Images" folder** (media-root-aware, so it migrates with everything else), and every reader (Video Assembly scan + duration bridge, Scene Review list/serve/approve/regenerate/upload, the Timestamp assembler, and the pending-approvals badge) resolves the **named folder first with a fallback to the legacy flat folder** — so existing un-consolidated episodes keep working untouched. No new `scene_images/` folders are created going forward. (Phase 2 — consolidating existing flat folders — is a manual copy you can do per episode, then delete the old folder once confirmed.)

## v1.0.456 — 2026-06-22

**Fixed: continuity scene images didn't show in Video Assembly when the project was made on another Mac/user.** Each scene in `scene_plan.json` stores an absolute `image_path` baked in at render time. On a different machine or macOS user that path points at a stale home directory (e.g. `/Users/theng/…` when this Mac is `/build/…`), so the existence check failed and **every** scene was silently dropped from Video Assembly — even though `scene_images/<id>.png` was sitting right there. Video Assembly now falls back to the local id-based path whenever the stored absolute path is missing (both when listing scenes and when applying the Scene-Plan durations), matching how Scene Review already resolved images. Affected KH Boundless EP13/14/15 and any project moved between Macs.

## v1.0.451 — 2026-06-21

### Added — opt-in external media root (foundation): heavy media can live off iCloud
Projects can now (optionally) keep their **light artifacts** — scripts, metadata, prompts, subtitles, sidecars, `project.json` — in the iCloud project tree while routing **heavy media** — scene images, thumbnails, audio, merged audio, final video — to a separate **media root**, typically an external SSD that isn't iCloud-synced. This stops episodes' 200–300 scene images (~300 MB+/episode) from filling iCloud, and lands b-roll/image-pool "load as scenes" files on the media root instead of duplicating into iCloud.

**Fully opt-in / default-off.** It's enabled per project by a new optional `media_root` in `project.json` — a portable Named-Root token like `${MEDIA}` (resolved per machine via Settings → Named Roots, so the same project works across Macs when you carry the SSD). **With no `media_root` set (the default), behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged** — everything stays under `output_root`. Anyone who wants everything on iCloud does nothing.

This release lands the **foundation** (steps 1–2 of the spec): the media-aware path resolver plus the main content-flow call sites (scene images, audio, merged audio, final video, the asset scan, status, and b-roll/image-pool materialize). The Settings UI, the one-time migration tool for existing episodes, fail-loud "drive not plugged in" preflight, and a few peripheral read sites (AI-video clips, manifest audit, reconciler) are tracked follow-ups. Until those land + a `media_root` is set, no behavior changes. See `docs/external-media-root-spec.md`.

### Files
- `electron/server/services/media-root.ts` (new — `HEAVY_SUBFOLDERS`, `resolveMediaBase`, `mediaEpisodeBaseForCode`, `resolveEpisodeSubfolderDir`/`findEpisodeSubfolderDir`)
- `electron/server/services/utils.ts` (`resolveEpisodePaths` routes heavy subfolders through `mediaBase`)
- `electron/server/models/types.ts` (`ProjectMeta.media_root?`)
- `electron/server/generators/{video,images,audio,audio-merge}.ts`, `services/asset-status.ts`, `routes/broll-project.ts` (call sites → media-aware)
- `electron/server/__tests__/media-root.test.ts` (new)

## v1.0.450 — 2026-06-21

**Fixed: manually clicking Re-stitch on the Subtitles page discarded an Audio Assembly intro offset.** Automatic stitching after transcription already measured the merged audio and shifted chapter cues past a prepended intro or music lead-in, but the manual route called the stitcher without that value and overwrote the correct timeline starting at zero. Both paths now share the same episode-level lead-in calculation, and the completion message reports the applied intro offset. Brain Wise EP0012 was repaired to begin captions at `27.989s`, matching its 26-second intro plus 2-second gap and the measured merged-audio timeline.

## v1.0.449 — 2026-06-21

**Fixed: Pipeline chapter expansion could silently drop the Script preset's POV and narrator style after producing the correct outline.** Outline sidecars now lock the selected perspective, custom POV note, and resolved narrator style alongside the model and word targets. Expand Chapters restores those settings before building its system prompt, and the Script page mirrors them back into the visible form and “Locked at outline build” summary instead of showing a misleading format default. This keeps presets such as Brain Wise's second-person immersive narration consistent from outline through every generated or resumed chapter.

**Fixed: renumbering an episode could create a second stale outline sidecar under the old episode code.** Renames now update the chunked-progress file's embedded episode ID, and sidecar reads defensively normalize older mismatched IDs to the filename being requested. Later expansion progress therefore continues writing only to the current episode sidecar instead of recreating an old-code duplicate.

## v1.0.448 — 2026-06-21

### Fixed — Pasting/importing a script now writes into the existing episode folder
When you used **Bring your own → Import script** (or Import outline) in the Script Generator, the destination folder was built from the *title in the form*. If that title didn't exactly match the title the episode folder was created with — a rename that never reached disk, copy-paste drift, or a `✅` done-marker prefix on the folder — the app created a **brand-new phantom folder** next to the real one instead of writing into it. At bulk-import scale that's a folder for every mismatch. Both import endpoints now resolve the real folder by **episode code** (`EP0110 - …`, `✅`-tolerant) the same way the image-prompt save path does, and only create a new folder when no episode matches that code.

### Files
- `electron/server/routes/scripts.ts` (new `resolveScriptDirForImport` helper used by `import-script` + `import-outline`; matches the on-disk folder by code via `resolveEpisodeDir` + `resolveSubfolder`)

## v1.0.447 — 2026-06-21

**Added: Thumbnail Prompts now combine a shared Visual Style with an independent Thumbnail Treatment.** The same built-in style gallery used by Character Sheet and Scene Plan can now define the artwork medium for thumbnails, while separate Bold Explainer, Cinematic Minimal, Cozy Story, Documentary Impact, and Text-Free Compose starters control composition, title treatment, hierarchy, and title-safe space. ## v1.0.446 — 2026-06-21

**Expanded: every generator concurrency control can now be raised to 50 without changing existing defaults.** Text/LLM jobs and expression tagging were capped at 8, video at 8, Audio settings reloaded values above 15 back down, and subtitle queue plumbing capped cross-job transcription at 3. Those ceilings now accept up to 50, matching the existing Image, Audio runtime, Subtitle per-job, and continuity-render pools. Defaults remain conservative: Text 2, Images 5, Audio 3, Video 2, and Subtitles Auto. Expression tagging now follows the selected global text concurrency for both local and cloud models, so a 12–15 chapter project can tag more than three chapters concurrently when configured.

## v1.0.445 — 2026-06-21

**Faster: Audio expression tagging now runs chapters concurrently and can spread local work across the LM Studio server pool.** Abiding Faith's three short prayer sections previously tagged one after another, so the least-busy local dispatcher never had simultaneous requests to distribute. Local models now use the machine's configured text concurrency (up to the number of chapters), while cloud models remain capped at three parallel requests. Background Tag All still saves each completed chapter through a serialized sidecar write, and hands-off Audio/Pipeline tagging uses the same bounded worker pool. The expression-tagging model is now part of the Audio preset, so selecting Gemma and saving the preset also carries that choice into unattended Pipeline audio instead of falling back to DeepSeek.

## v1.0.444 — 2026-06-21

**Fixed: Metadata presets did not save or restore their AI model.** The preset name could say Local or DeepSeek, but only the description sections and title settings were stored; batch generation then hardcoded `deepseek-v4-flash` regardless of the model shown on the Metadata page. New and re-saved presets now include the shared AI model, Apply restores it in the picker, and Pipeline jobs use that saved model. Older presets remain valid and keep the existing DeepSeek fallback until re-saved.

## v1.0.443 — 2026-06-21

**Fixed: selecting an episode could overwrite the Script preset with one enormous chapter.** Episode suggestions such as `10 min` were only checked for an exact `60 min` value, so every other duration silently became 45 minutes. Abiding Faith's older one-chapter episode records therefore became `1 × 5,850 words` at 130 words/minute, replacing the intended `3 × 1,000` Script preset. Saved preset sizing is now treated as explicit user intent, real minute values are parsed correctly, and stale episode chapter counts outside the active format/niche range fall back to the current effective structure.

## v1.0.442 — 2026-06-20

**Fixed: fade-to-black could still create a microscopic black hold after the v1.0.440 timing fix.** The total post-audio tail was already clamped to whole video frames, but subtracting an exact 5-second fade from a value such as `5.000000000000455` seconds left a second floating-point remainder for the derived black hold. That inner hold duration is now frame-clamped too, preventing the DK0027 `color=black...d=4.547e-13` failure after a long render.

## v1.0.441 — 2026-06-20

**Expanded: B-Roll auto-tagging now uses the full shared AI model catalog.** The model picker is grouped by provider and includes every available OpenAI vision model plus all live LM Studio models, so local vision models can tag images and video frames for free. Models without a configured key and text-only models remain visible with a clear disabled reason. DeepSeek is shown as text-only because its current API models cannot inspect images; the backend now rejects an explicit text-only selection instead of silently falling back to GPT-4o.

## v1.0.440 — 2026-06-20

**Fixed: Video Assembly could fail after a long render when timeline math left a microscopic post-audio remainder.** A scene timeline that matched the target duration could differ by a tiny floating-point amount (such as `4.5e-13` seconds), causing FFmpeg to reject an effectively zero-length black, fade, or hold clip. Post-audio durations shorter than one video frame are now treated as zero, so correctly fitted timelines proceed directly to final composition.

## v1.0.439 — 2026-06-20

**Added: import extra images and video clips directly into Video Assembly.** Step 1 now has an **Add images/videos** action that copies selected media into the episode's reusable scene pool, assigns safe scene numbers, rescans immediately, and uses the normal shuffle and recycling behavior. Episodes with Scene Plan renders automatically switch to the Combined pool so imported assets are available without episode-specific code or timeline changes.

## v1.0.438 — 2026-06-20

**Fixed: animated subtitles truncated long lines with "…" and dropped the rest of the sentence.** When caption animation is on (fade / pop / slide-up), each cue was wrapped to your `max_lines × max_chars` and any overflow was cut off with an ellipsis — so a line like *"you are invited into the refuge of God's…"* lost everything after "God's", and that text never appeared anywhere in the video. Now an over-long cue is **split into multiple sequential captions** across its own time window instead of truncated, so every spoken word is shown (the line/char limits are still respected per caption). The non-animated path was already fine (libass wraps without dropping text).

## v1.0.437 — 2026-06-20

**Fixed: turning a Mac OFF in Settings now actually removes it from the render/audio pool — including mid-render.** The per-Mac on/off switch was only honoured by the single-image path. The parallel batch generators (Scene Generator's multi-Mac pool, the continuity renderer, and the Voice Studio audio pool) built their pool from *network reachability only* — so a Mac you switched off but left powered on kept getting work. Now all of them build the pool from **enabled** endpoints, and the periodic re-probe (every ~20s) re-reads the switch each cycle, so a Mac you disable **during** a long generation is dropped from rotation within one probe cycle (a disabled Mac is also never contacted). Re-enabling a still-running pool's Mac brings it back when it's reachable.

## v1.0.436 — 2026-06-20

**Fixed: Scene/Thumbnail generation could read a stale Word file instead of the current Markdown prompts.** The prompts-file resolver was supposed to prefer the modern `.md` over a legacy `.docx`, but it actually returned whichever file the OS listed first — and `.docx` sorts before `.md` alphabetically. So if an episode had *both* `<code>_Scene_Prompts.md` (the up-to-date prompts) and an old `<code>_Scene_Prompts.docx` left over from an earlier run, the generator parsed the **stale `.docx`** and only generated that many scenes. This is exactly why Dozing Knight DK0028 generated only 12 scenes despite having 240 prompts in the `.md`. The resolver now honours the preference order (`.md` always wins) for both scene prompts and thumbnail prompts. Re-run Scene Generator and it'll pick up the full prompt set.

## v1.0.435 — 2026-06-20

**Continuity scene renders now show in Video Assembly without needing approval.** Video Assembly merges scene-plan renders (`scene_images/<id>.png`) into the scene pool alongside classic numbered images — but it used to skip any scene not marked *approved* in Scene Review. Classic images were never approval-gated, so this was inconsistent: a project that rendered hundreds of continuity scenes but never clicked through approval saw none of them. Now **any plan scene with a rendered image on disk shows up** (the Scene Plan / Classic / Combined toggle still picks which set renders, and Auto defaults to the plan renders). This is what unblocks projects that switched format mid-way — e.g. Dozing Knight, which had 366 continuity renders invisible because they weren't approved.

## v1.0.430 — 2026-06-19

### Audited — Video Assembly still/video handling and timeline duration
Video Assembly's complete visual path was audited after the B-Roll loop failures: scene preparation, title input, transitions, recycling, exclusions, chapter alignment, post-audio tails, overlays, concat, and final duration.

The audit fixed four connected issues:

- **Post-audio tails now use the real last played scene.** Fade and hold previously used the last numbered request scene, which could be wrong after exclusions, shuffle, chapter alignment, or extra transition-coverage clips.
- **Fade and hold freeze the actual final frame.** Video scenes no longer restart from their beginning during the post-audio tail.
- **Crossfades cannot end visuals before narration.** Transition overlap is included in coverage calculations; extra clips are added only when needed, surplus repeats are removed, and only the final played clip is trimmed to the exact narration boundary. This preserves the configured fade/hold tail instead of letting scene overshoot hide it.
- **Looping overlays are media-aware.** PNG/JPEG overlays use FFmpeg's still-image loop option, while video, GIF, and other stream inputs use `-stream_loop`.

Verification covered 53 Video Assembly/FFmpeg regression tests, production frontend and Electron builds, exact EP0075 duration math, and real FFmpeg smoke renders for scene trimming, final-frame extraction, fade generation, still overlay looping, and variable-duration crossfades.

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/video.ts` (timeline fitting, actual final-frame tails, shared media classification, overlay input handling)
- `electron/server/__tests__/video-encode-argv.test.ts` (media and transition-duration regression coverage)

## v1.0.429 — 2026-06-19

### Fixed — B-Roll video works in post-audio fade and hold tails
The `v1.0.428` title fix allowed MP4 scenes to be used as title assets, but Video Assembly had two additional still-image assumptions after scene concatenation. The **Fade to black** and **Hold last scene** post-audio modes reopened the final B-Roll scene with FFmpeg's image-only `-loop 1` option, causing `Option loop not found` after several minutes of successful scene preparation.

All bounded looping visual inputs now share media-aware argument generation: still images use `-loop 1`, while MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, and M4V files use `-stream_loop -1`. This fixes EP0075 and other B-Roll assemblies whose final scene is a video.

Video Assembly could automatically seed its Title Image field from a materialized B-Roll scene. When that asset was an MP4, the title preparation stage still passed FFmpeg's still-image-only `-loop 1` option, causing assembly to fail with `Option loop not found`.

## v1.0.426 — 2026-06-19

### Fixed — Video Assembly can use Classic and Scene Plan images after a format change
Episodes that had both classic numbered scene images and reviewed Scene Plan renders only exposed the classic folder in Video Assembly. The scanner treated Scene Plan as a fallback and loaded it only when the classic scene folder was empty, so changing a finished episode to the Scenes format hid hundreds of approved planned renders.

Video Assembly now scans both sources without moving or copying their files:

- **Scene Plan** uses the approved reviewed renders and preserves their exact planned durations.
- **Classic** uses the numbered images from the episode's Scene Images folder.
- **Combined** exposes both sources in one scene pool with unique pool numbers.
- When both exist, Video Assembly defaults to Scene Plan so an existing reviewed timeline is not silently changed.

For Dozing Knight DK0026 this exposes 12 Classic scenes, 536 approved Scene Plan scenes, and 548 scenes in Combined mode.

## v1.0.423 — 2026-06-19

**Sleep-story intro handling — scenes skip the Introduction, title card holds through it.** For formats whose first audio chapter is the spoken **Introduction** (welcome / context / CTA / breathing), there's now a per-project toggle on the **Scene Plan** page: *"Skip the Introduction chapter when planning scenes."* When on:
- **Scene planning** ignores the Introduction transcript, so scenes are generated only for the actual story — no more off-topic intro scenes.
- **Video render** auto-holds your **title (thumbnail) card** through the intro: it computes where the story starts (lead-in + Introduction + gap) and holds the card for exactly `story_start − intro-video length`. Make your intro video longer and the title hold shrinks to match — the first story scene always lands on its narration.
- **Intro captions are hidden by default** (you wanted the welcome/CTA/breathing uncaptioned). The burned-in track drops cues before the story; the full SRT sidecar for YouTube upload is untouched. Toggle it per episode in Video Assembly → Subtitles → *"Hide captions during the intro."*

The skip point and the title hold derive from the **same** computed story-start, so visuals, captions, and audio stay in lockstep. Also fixes a latent bug where the effects-gate start assumed a fixed 5s title duration (it now reads the title clip's real length, which matters once the card is held for 60s+).

## v1.0.419 — 2026-06-18

### Changed — Video export defaults to Apple hardware acceleration on capable Macs
On Macs whose FFmpeg build exposes Apple's Media Engine encoder (`h264_videotoolbox` — i.e. Apple Silicon and other modern Macs), Video Assembly now **defaults to the hardware-accelerated H.264 path** instead of the CPU encoder. For the renders this app produces — ~20-minute videos from ~300 stills — that's roughly **8–15× faster** (a render that took ~30–40 min on libx264 `medium` finishes in a few minutes) with **no visible quality loss** on mostly-static footage. The output format is unchanged: still 1920×1080 H.264 MP4 with `-pix_fmt yuv420p`, `-movflags +faststart`, and AAC 192k audio. Constant-quality `-q:v` is preserved (no switch to fixed bitrate). The encoder presence **is** the platform check — where `h264_videotoolbox` isn't in the build (Linux/Windows, older Macs, brewed builds without VideoToolbox) the libx264 default is left untouched. This only seeds the form default: a saved export preset / bundle still wins, and you can drop to any CPU preset in one click.

### Changed — Hardware-encode failures now fall back without losing effects
If a hardware (VideoToolbox) encode fails to initialise mid-render, the recovery chain now re-encodes the **full filter graph** on the CPU with libx264 (matching the quality tier's preset) before resorting to the bare-bones "minimal" recovery. Previously a transient VideoToolbox failure dropped straight to the minimal tier and stripped every post effect (grain/grade/chroma/subtitles/logo); now those are preserved — the fallback is just slower, not degraded.

### Files
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/video-assembly.vue` (`applyHardwareExportDefaultIfAvailable` seeds `encoding_effort: 'hardware'` in `onMounted` before presets load; `ffmpegStatus` ref type now carries `hw_encoders`)
- `electron/server/generators/video.ts` (`encoderArgs`/`buildFullArgs` accept an effort override; new "hardware → libx264 full effects" recovery tier in `runFinalComposition`)

## v1.0.416 — 2026-06-17

### Fixed / Added — thumbnails now always carry the title + ratio, plus inline render guidance
Two thumbnail problems addressed:

**1. Prompts that ignored the title and aspect ratio.** The LLM was *already* told to include the literal title, the aspect ratio, and "this is a YouTube cover, not a scene still" — but models routinely paraphrased it ("Title text in monospace font…" with no actual title words) or dropped the ratio entirely, so ~half the renders came out with random/no text. The generator now **enforces these deterministically**: after the model returns each thumbnail prompt, the chosen **aspect ratio + "YouTube thumbnail" framing** is guaranteed, and in **AI (baked-text) mode** the **literal episode title in quotes** is guaranteed — appending only what the model left out (no bloat when it already complied). **Composite (text-free) mode is untouched** so its background stays clean for the overlay. Applied to both first-generation **and** per-row Reprompt/Regenerate; the instruction wording was tightened too.

**2. No way to nudge a render without reprompting.** The **Thumbnail Generator** tab now has an **"Extra details for this render"** box. Whatever you type is appended to the prompt for that generation — per-row or "Generate All" — e.g. *"push the subject closer, bigger title, warmer lighting"* — with no prompt-edit / reprompt round-trip.

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/image-prompts.ts` (new `enforceThumbnailPromptElements`, applied post-parse; tightened directive + requirements)
- `electron/server/routes/image-prompts-edit.ts` (enforce on Reprompt/Regenerate, with safe composite inference)
- `electron/server/generators/images.ts`, `contracts/index.ts`, `models/types.ts` (`extra_details` appended at render time)

## v1.0.415 — 2026-06-17

### Added — B-roll clips can play their full natural length
Until now every scene — stills **and** B-roll video clips — was held on screen for the uniform **Seconds Per Scene** (Step 3 → Scene Recycling): a video clip was stream-looped and trimmed to that length rather than playing for its own duration.

There's now a tick in **Scene Recycling**: **"Play B-roll clips at their full natural length."** When on, each B-roll **video** scene is probed and plays for its **own natural duration** (once, no loop); **still images are unaffected** and keep the per-scene length. The render log reports how many video scenes used their natural length. It's **off by default** (existing presets are byte-for-byte unchanged), saved with your Video Assembly presets, and honoured by Pipeline batch runs.

Note: with it on, B-roll no longer syncs to narration timing (it plays whole clips, and the usual cycling still repeats scenes to fill the narration). If your natural clips are very short, keep crossfades short — transitions are clamped to `Seconds Per Scene − 0.5`.

## v1.0.413 — 2026-06-17

### Fixed — subtitle preview now matches the rendered video (font sizing)
The subtitle preview looked different from the final render — especially **font size**. Root cause: libass interprets `FontSize` relative to the *frame's own resolution*, but the "Render exact preview" rendered at **640×360** while the final video renders at **1080p**, so the same size looked much bigger in the preview than in the export. The CSS live preview also used a fixed `0.42` fudge factor unrelated to the actual preview size.

Fixes:
- **Pinned libass to a fixed 1080 reference** (`original_size=1920x1080`) in the final render *and* the exact preview, so `FontSize` means "pixels at 1080" everywhere. The exact preview now matches the final render proportionally, and subtitle sizing is now **consistent across export resolutions** (720p/1080p/4k). For 1080p exports (the default) the rendered output is unchanged.
- **CSS live preview** now scales the font by the preview frame's *actual measured height ÷ 1080* (via a ResizeObserver) instead of the hardcoded factor — so what you see tracks the real size.

Net: the preview — both the instant CSS one and "Render exact preview" — now reflects the burned-in result, font size included.

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/video.ts` (final render + exact-preview: `original_size=1920x1080`)
- `electron/server/generators/broll-assemble.ts` (final render: `original_size=1920x1080`)
- `frontend/components/SubtitleStylePicker.vue` (CSS preview scales by measured frame height ÷ 1080)

## v1.0.400 — 2026-06-17

### Fixed — Subtitles: "audio_chapters.json not found — Run Audio Assembly first" now self-heals
Episodes merged on an older build (before the chapter-duration sidecar was written reliably) could **never stitch their subtitles** — Stitch and auto-stitch both dead-ended with *"audio_chapters.json not found"*, even though every per-chapter audio file and per-chapter SRT was sitting right there. Re-running Audio Assembly would write the sidecar, but it also **re-creates the merged audio**, which risks desyncing scenes you've already rendered.

Now the stitcher **rebuilds the missing sidecar from the chapter audio on disk** instead of forcing a re-merge:
- It measures each chapter file (folding multi-part chapters into one section, like Audio Assembly does) and **derives the inter-chapter gap** from `merged duration − sum of chapters`. That's exact to a few hundredths of a second across a whole episode, so the stitched timing lines up.
- It writes the reconstructed `audio_chapters.json` (tagged `"reconstructed": true`) so it's healed for next time and the chapter-aligned video assembler finds it too.
- Falls back to a 5 s gap only if the merged audio is also gone, and stays a no-op when the sidecar already exists.

Both the **Stitch subtitles** button and the **auto-stitch after transcribe** use it, so old episodes recover on the next stitch with no re-merge. (For a perfectly exact gap you can still re-run Audio Assembly — but you no longer have to.)

This was never the recent updates' fault, and it isn't format-specific — the sidecar code runs for every merge; these episodes just predate a clean write.

### Files
- `electron/server/lib/audio-chapters-reconstruct.ts` (new — `buildReconstructedSidecar` / `reconstructAudioChapters` / `ensureAudioChaptersSidecar`)
- `electron/server/routes/scene-plan.ts` (stitch route self-heals first)
- `electron/server/generators/subtitles.ts` (auto-stitch self-heals first)
- `electron/server/__tests__/audio-chapters-reconstruct.test.ts`

## v1.0.399 — 2026-06-16

### Fixed — effects, logo overlay, and subtitles silently dropped from the final video
When effects were time-gated to start after the intro (Effects & Overlays → "exclude intro from effects"), the `enable='gt(t,…)'` gate was being appended to **every** filter in the composition — including FFmpeg's libass subtitle filters (`ass` / `subtitles`). Those filters **don't support** the timeline `enable` option, so FFmpeg failed to initialise the whole filtergraph (`Timeline ('enable' option) not supported with filter 'ass'`). The encoder then fell back to its no-effects **recovery tier**, producing a clean video with the colour grade, vignette, film grain, chroma key, **logo overlay**, and **subtitles** all stripped — even though every one of them was configured. The job still reported success, so the loss was silent.

The fix: the two libass subtitle filters no longer receive the gate (the other gated filters — `eq`, `colorbalance`, `vignette`, `noise`, `overlay` — keep it; they support it). Keeping captions off the intro was already handled the right way — the stitched SRT's cue timestamps are offset past the intro lead-in (v1.0.398), so no cues ever fell inside the gated window. Effects renders now complete on the full-effects tier instead of silently dropping to recovery.

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/video.ts` (drop `gateEnable` from the `ass` / `subtitles` libass filters; correct the `buildGateEnable` doc comment that wrongly listed `subtitles` as gate-compatible)

## v1.0.398 — 2026-06-16

### Fixed — subtitles ignored the intro audio, so captions ran ahead of the video
When Audio Assembly starts the merged track with a lead-in before the narration — a prepended **intro file + gap**, or the new (v1.0.397) **background-music lead-in** that delays the voice — the subtitle timelines built from the **clean per-chapter narration** (the stitched `_stitched.srt` and the "Auto from chapters" `_chapters.srt`) still started at `00:00:00`, so every caption ran **ahead of the video by the lead-in length**. That's the mismatch.

The subtitle builders now detect the **intro lead-in** and offset the whole timeline by it. It's computed read-only as `merged-audio duration − narration extent` — the merge has no outro, so that difference is exactly the lead-in, **whichever way it was produced** (intro file or the music lead-in from 1.0.397). Nothing in the Audio Assembly / merge code is touched; intro-less episodes compute a 0 offset and are byte-for-byte unchanged. The detected value is logged ("intro lead-in 12.0s applied").

To apply it to an episode you already transcribed: **re-run "Transcribe (Whisper)"** (the auto-stitch re-applies it) or click **"Auto from chapters"** again. The merged-audio Whisper SRT (`_whisper.srt`) was already correct (Whisper times against the merged file directly) and is unchanged. Scene Plan's stitch passes no lead-in, so scene timing is unaffected.

### Files
- `electron/server/lib/intro-lead-in.ts` (new — `computeIntroLeadInSec`)
- `electron/server/services/subtitle-stitcher.ts` (optional `lead_in_sec` → timeline start offset)
- `electron/server/generators/subtitles.ts` (auto-stitch computes + applies the lead-in)
- `electron/server/lib/subtitle-builder.ts` (`chaptersFromDurations` start-offset param)
- `electron/server/routes/video.ts` ("from chapters" derivation applies + reports the lead-in)

## v1.0.396 — 2026-06-16

### Fixed — B-Roll burned the wrong subtitle file; now you can pick (+ smarter auto)
When an episode had several subtitle files on disk (e.g. a full `EP0075_stitched.srt` plus per-chapter `EP0075_Chapter_01/02/03.srt`), the B-Roll assembler burned **the first `.srt` in directory order** — which on macOS is alphabetical, so `Chapter_01` beat `stitched` and you got only the first chapter's captions, with **no way to choose**. Good catch.

Two fixes:
- **You can now pick the file to burn.** The "Subtitle files on disk" list has a radio per file plus an **Auto** option; your pick is persisted per-episode (a `.selected_subtitle` sidecar in the episode's subtitles folder) and the next assembly burns exactly that one. The selected row shows **✓ burned next**.
- **Smarter Auto.** When nothing is pinned, Auto now prefers a full transcript — `*_stitched` → `*_whisper` → any non-per-chapter file — and only falls back to a `Chapter_NN` partial if that's all there is. So even without picking, it stops burning Chapter 1 by accident.

The same resolver is shared so the burn target is consistent. The B-Roll assembler change is otherwise unchanged (still skips burn entirely when subtitles are disabled).

### Files
- `electron/server/lib/subtitle-selection.ts` (new — pin sidecar read/write + `resolveBurnSubtitle` auto-heuristic)
- `electron/server/generators/broll-assemble.ts` (use `resolveBurnSubtitle` instead of first-match)
- `electron/server/routes/video.ts` (status returns `selected_subtitle`; new `PUT …/subtitles/select/:episodeId`)

## v1.0.394 — 2026-06-15

### Improved — cross-device file paths now survive Mac-to-Mac project handoff much better
If your project lives in iCloud Drive and you switch between Macs with different home usernames, several production pages could still save raw absolute paths like `/Users/you/...`. That meant a preset, remembered field, logo, subtitle import, or assembly asset could look fine on one Mac and silently break on the next.

- **Audio Assembly and Video Assembly now normalize many picked/saved asset paths into portable project-aware paths** instead of storing machine-specific absolute ones.
- **Preset path validation now resolves portable paths correctly**, so "broken path" warnings are based on the current Mac's real location rather than the original machine's username.
- **Preview routes now understand portable paths**, so audio/image previews still open after a device switch.
- The shared **`FilePicker`** now supports project-aware portable path normalization, and key pages now use it:
  - **Video Assembly** intro/outro/title image/logo/chroma/timeline clips
  - **Timestamp Assembly** music + ambient beds
  - **Subtitles** import
  - **B-Roll** subtitle import
  - **Brand** logo selection
- **Image Prompts** now portableize the saved reference-image path too, including edited references and reloaded remembered references.
- **Thumbnail Compose** now saves the per-project channel logo path in portable form as well.

Net effect: the app is much less likely to break just because one Mac is `/build` and another is `/Users/othername`.

### Fixed — local subtitle transcription no longer falls back to OpenAI on retry / merged-audio paths
The subtitle transcription flow had two bad edge cases around the Voice Studio engine:

- a merged-audio transcription could still route through **OpenAI Whisper** even when the user had chosen **Voice Studio (local)**, which could either bill OpenAI unexpectedly or fail with an opaque invalid-model error
- a partial local-pool failure could throw away a mostly-successful episode instead of keeping the chapters that already transcribed

Now:

- **Voice Studio stays on the local Whisper pool** for the merged-audio path too
- **OpenAI rejects local-only Whisper repo ids with a clear message** instead of surfacing a vague 400
- **Per-chapter local failures are isolated**, so successful chapter SRTs are kept and only the failed chapters need a re-run
- **Chapter audio discovery is more robust** when audio exists on disk but chunk/version naming differs from the old predictor
- **Retry preserves the subtitle engine details properly**, so a Voice Studio job retries as Voice Studio instead of mutating into an OpenAI-shaped request

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/subtitles.ts`, `electron/server/lib/whisper-client.ts`, `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/jobs.vue`
- `electron/server/routes/{system,video,audio-merge}.ts`
- `frontend/components/FilePicker.vue`, `frontend/components/ThumbnailComposeDialog.vue`
- `frontend/composables/{usePresetPathValidation,useVideoAssemblyIo}.ts`
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/{audio-merge,video-assembly,image-prompts,timestamp-assemble,subtitles,broll}.vue`
- `frontend/pages/brands/[id].vue`
