## v1.0.393 — 2026-06-14

### Improved — Thumbnail prompts now push for deliberate title treatment, not just a pretty scene
Two recent Terranash sleep-story episodes surfaced a regression in the newer format-aware thumbnail flow: the prompt could still come back as a strong scenic image description, but it wasn't forceful enough about the **title being a core design element**. That made some thumbnail prompts feel like "good scene prompt, weak cover brief" — especially when using strong image models like GPT Image 2 / Nano Banana that don't need generic help and benefit more from a precise, professional thumbnail brief.

- **Thumbnail prompt requests are now much stricter about cover design.** The generator explicitly asks for a professional YouTube cover, not a scene still, and requires the prompt to describe the **hero subject, emotional hook, framing, negative space, background separation, lighting direction, color contrast, and why the title area stays readable**.
- **AI-title mode is stronger.** When the title should be rendered inside the image, the request now tells the model to treat the title as a **core design element**, with composition / lighting / contrast built around making it premium and legible.
- **Composite-title mode is clearer.** Text-free thumbnail prompts now explicitly describe a **reserved text-safe zone**, so the generated background feels intentionally designed for a later overlay instead of accidentally empty.
- **Single-row thumbnail review is now much better.** In Thumbnail Prompts / Scene Prompts, each row can now be **expanded, previewed, edited inline, saved back to disk, and reprompted with feedback notes**. That means if a prompt feels too scenic / not clicky enough, you can steer just that one row without regenerating everything.
- **Shared DMG copies now keep the version in the filename.** The post-release iCloud copy no longer strips the version off the DMG name, so you can see exactly which build you're installing.

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/image-prompts.ts` (stronger thumbnail brief + title-treatment wording)
- `electron/server/routes/image-prompts-edit.ts` (single-row save API + richer reprompt input)
- `frontend/components/PromptReviewPanel.vue`, `frontend/components/PromptReviewPanelRow.vue` (inline preview/edit/save/reprompt flow)

### Improved — Image generator now shows live pool joins/offline changes during local runs
The regular Image Generator already used the multi-Mac Image Studio pool for parallel renders, but unlike Scene Review it only logged the **startup** health snapshot. If a Mac came online mid-run, or one dropped off, the Jobs panel stayed quiet even though the pool was self-healing underneath.

- **Live `N/N` pool updates now appear in the job log** during scene/thumbnail generation, including which Macs **joined** and which went **offline**.
- **Worker count now follows the live pool** during a run, so newly-online Macs can start taking work without waiting for a fresh job.
- The **Image Generation Concurrency** setting also now reloads correctly up to **50** instead of snapping back to the old stale `10` cap after refresh.

### Fixed — release copy now removes the stale unversioned iCloud DMG
The shared iCloud folder still had an older legacy installer name:

- `Story Studio KH-arm64.dmg`

That stale unversioned file could sit beside the newer versioned build and make it look like the shared installer hadn't updated. The post-release copy step now removes that legacy file and its sidecar automatically, leaving the current versioned DMG as the source of truth.

### Files

- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/settings.vue` (reload cap 10 → 50)

## v1.0.388 — 2026-06-14

### Added — ElevenLabs v3 expression + auto-pause (your other main model)
Emotion markup and auto-pause now work on **ElevenLabs v3** too, not just Fish S2-Pro. Pick an **ElevenLabs v3** model (`eleven-v3` via fal, or `genaipro-v3` via GenAIPro) and the Expression panel + auto-pause appear, speaking ElevenLabs' own tag dialect:

- **ElevenLabs tags** use the verb form — `[whispers]`, `[laughs]`, `[sighs]`, `[excited]`, `[sarcastic]`, `[pause]` — vs Fish's `[whispering]` / `[long pause]`. The AI pass, the quick-insert chips, and auto-pause all switch automatically based on the selected model.

- Expressiveness (temperature) stays Fish-only — ElevenLabs doesn't expose it via these gateways.

Everything from the Fish flow carries over to ElevenLabs v3: review/edit, the tag toolbar, background "Tag all", and the hands-off Pipeline auto-tagging.

## v1.0.387 — 2026-06-14

### Added — Pipeline auto-tags emotion (hands-off Fish expression)
When a Fish S2-Pro audio render has **Use expression markup** on but a section hasn't been tagged yet, the audio job now **generates the markup on the fly** (and saves it for reuse) instead of falling back to plain narration. So a Pipeline or remote-cockpit batch is fully hands-off: if your saved audio preset has expression on, every episode gets emotion + pacing automatically — no need to open each one and hit "Tag all" first.

## v1.0.379 — 2026-06-14

### Fixed — Fish Audio "Test" button reported "Unknown provider"
Saving a Fish Audio key worked and audio generation worked, but the **Test** button in Settings → API Keys errored with *"Unknown provider: fishaudio"* — the key-test path had no Fish case. It now probes Fish's wallet endpoint and reports **"Key works — N credit remaining"** (Fish bills in credit bytes, so the number is shown neutrally, not as dollars). An invalid key reads "Invalid key (401)".

### Fixed — Scene Review (and Scene Plan / Subtitles / Final Video) crashed when run from the Pipeline
Running **Scene Review (render)** from the Pipeline always errored out. The batch runner enqueued each step under its own id, but four steps use a *different* job type internally — Scene Review renders via `continuity_render`, Scene Plan via `scene_plan_run`, Subtitles via `subtitles_transcribe`, and Final Video (timestamp) via `timestamp_video_assemble`. The id mismatch was hidden by a type cast, so at run time the queue had no lane for `scene_review` and threw before the job could start (a chained Scene Review instead logged "Chain-next failed" and silently stopped).

- The Pipeline now translates each step to its real job type before queueing, so **Scene Review, Scene Plan, Subtitles, and Final Video all run from the Pipeline.**
- Scene Review from the Pipeline runs in **independent / parallel mode across your Mac pool** at the preset's concurrency — this *is* the "parallel render" path; there's no separate toggle needed.
- It now also honors the preset's **render mode** (`Prompt only` → text-to-image, no reference images). Render *size* (`render_scale`) is local-model-only and falls back to the model's aspect-default resolution in batch runs.
- A regression test pins that every Pipeline step maps to a real job-queue lane, so a future mismatched step fails the build instead of the user.

### Files
- `electron/server/services/utils.ts` (Fish Audio key-test probe)
- `electron/server/routes/pipeline.ts` (step→JobType map + `jobTypeForStep`; thread `prompt_only` into Scene Review)
- `electron/server/services/job-queue.ts` (`knownJobTypes()` introspection)
- `electron/server/__tests__/pipeline-step-skip.test.ts` (lane-mapping regression)

### Fixed — Scene Review loads saved plans even with old scene-review job records
Scene Review could still show the empty **No scene plan yet** state for finished episodes because the review API crashed after reading `scene_plan.json`. The crash came from optional job metadata: old `jobs.json` files could contain retired `scene_review` job records, and `getJobs()` tried to calculate queue position from a queue lane that no longer exists.

## v1.0.373 — 2026-06-13

### Fixed — scene and thumbnail prompt/image generation are fully independent
The split from earlier releases still left one root-level escape hatch: Pipeline's single prompt step could still mean "both scene + thumbnail prompts" for classic scene-image projects, and the old unified image route still accepted `mode: "all"`. That made the app feel like the scene generator had only been renamed instead of truly separated.

This release removes the merged path:

- Pipeline now has separate **Thumbnail Prompts** and **Scene Prompts** steps.
- The Pipeline thumbnail prompt step always enqueues `image_prompts` with `mode: "thumbnails"`.
- The Pipeline scene prompt step always enqueues `image_prompts` with `mode: "scenes"`.
- Classic scene-image projects now run `Thumbnail Prompts → Thumbnails → Scene Prompts → Scene Images` as separate chain links.
- Pipeline no longer accepts the legacy unified `images` step in batch runs.
- `/generate/images` now accepts only `mode: "scenes"` or `mode: "thumbs"`; merged `mode: "all"` is rejected.
- `/generate/image-prompts` now accepts only `mode: "scenes"` or `mode: "thumbnails"`; explicit `mode: "all"` is rejected and missing mode defaults to thumbnails.
- Remote cockpit chains now include the separate Scene Prompts step for classic scene-image projects.
- Regression tests now pin the rule that scene prompts/images and thumbnail prompts/images are independent.

### Files
- `electron/server/routes/pipeline.ts`, `electron/server/routes/images.ts`, and `electron/server/routes/scripts.ts` (split-only batch/route contracts)
- `electron/server/generators/image-prompts.ts` and `electron/server/generators/images.ts` (reject merged all-mode generation)
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/pipeline.vue`, `frontend/composables/useRemoteChain.ts`, and generator pages (split-only UI flow)
- Pipeline route/unit tests and route validation tests (new split assertions)

The visual style was settable in two disconnected places — the Scene Plan "Style prompt" (plan-time) and the Character Sheet "Style Bible" (render-time) — which is the same idea applied at two stages. They're now unified around a single channel **Look**.

## v1.0.363 — 2026-06-13

### Changed — Pipeline automation now runs the whole audio-paced chain, not just the legacy front half
The batch Pipeline was stuck on the old sleep-story shape: it gated on **Script + Introduction**, and everything past Audio Merge (Scene Plan, Scene Review, the final timestamp render — and Subtitles, which wasn't even there) was a read-only "Open page →" note you had to run by hand. For the current formats that's all redundant manual clicking. This release rewires it end-to-end.

**Gate on the Script only.** Introduction is now **optional and off by default** — it was a sleep-story convention and nothing downstream needs it. **Metadata now depends on the Script alone** (it summarises the script; the intro was never an input). So one click no longer drags an intro step into every run.

**The Script step now runs your real outline-first flow.** Instead of the legacy one-shot, the batch runs **Outline → Expand Chapters**, both auto-approved — exactly what you do by hand on the Scripts page and get 100% acceptance on with a good model. (Point the Script preset at a paid/strong model; local models are where outline quality falls down.)

**Four steps were promoted from "Open page →" notes to real chained steps**, so a single "Run all the way to final video" click does the whole audio-paced pipeline:
- **Subtitles** — transcribes per-chapter SRTs (new step, slots in right after Audio Merge).
- **Character Sheet** — config-only, so the batch **writes `continuity.json` from your saved whole-page preset** inline (no job) before planning, so the planner + renderer see the anchor. Skipped cleanly if you haven't saved a preset.
- **Scene Plan** — runs `scene_plan_run` with your saved default attributes.
- **Scene Review (render)** — renders **every** planned scene image across your server pool (your model + concurrency preset). Uncheck the **Final Video** step if you'd rather stop here and eyeball the images first.
- **Final Video (timestamp)** — `timestamp_video_assemble`. Since there's no human at Scene Review in a full run, it **auto-approves every rendered scene** before assembling (the missing-image check still guards an incomplete render). Runs on built-in export defaults — no preset needed; tune it on its page.

Each step still skips when its output already exists (so a half-done episode only runs the gaps), `force` still re-runs everything, and the per-format chains only show the steps that format actually uses.

### Files
- `electron/server/routes/pipeline.ts` (new BatchSteps + preset keys + skip truth-table + param resolvers; script-only → outline_only/expand_chapters expansion; inline character-sheet apply; `character_sheets_applied` in the response)
- `electron/server/routes/continuity.ts` (extracted `buildContinuityConfig` / `writeContinuityConfig`, reused by the Character-Sheet step)

## v1.0.362 — 2026-06-13

### Fixed — Audited every "Pending only" filter; B-Roll and Video Assembly were keyed to the wrong step
You'd been finding these one tab at a time (Subtitles, then Character Sheet) — each had its **Pending only** filter secretly keyed to the wrong status field, so the list either hid every episode or showed all of them. Rather than wait to discover the rest, I swept **all 15** generator pages that have a Pending filter and checked each one against the step it actually produces. Eleven were already correct; two were wrong:

- **B-Roll** was keyed to `video` (AI per-scene clips) — but the stock-footage flow never produces those, so **every** episode looked pending, forever. Now there's a real signal: a **new `broll_picked` status field**, true once you've **picked a B-Roll selection** (`broll-selection.json` exists at the episode folder, written by the Pick route). "Pending only" now shows exactly the episodes you haven't selected clips for yet.
- **Video Assembly (timestamp flow)** was keyed to `video` too; it now keys to `video_assembly` — the final-render step it actually does. Continuity/timestamp episodes have no per-scene AI clips, so the old key never flipped.

`broll_picked` is optional like Research / Scene Plan / Character Sheet — it shows as a per-episode step chip when present, and is **not** folded into an episode's "all done" rollup. (B-Roll pick isn't a Production Board flow step, so it gets a chip but no board column.)

The takeaway: this whole **class** of bug — a Pending filter pointing at a proxy field instead of the page's own step — is now swept clean across the app, so you shouldn't keep tripping over new ones.

### Files
- `electron/server/services/asset-status.ts` (`broll_picked` field + detection via `broll-selection.json`; `emptyStatus`/`allDoneStatus`)

## v1.0.360 — 2026-06-13

### Fixed — Subtitles: switching episodes left Transcribe stuck on "loading/pending"
Switching episodes on the Subtitles tab could leave the page stuck showing the previous episode's loading/queueing state, so you couldn't queue a transcribe for the new one. Three fixes:
- **Race-guarded status load** — a slow status fetch from the episode you just left can no longer clobber the new episode's status or leave "Checking subtitle status…" stuck on.
- **Reset the queue flag on switch** — an in-flight transcribe POST on the previous episode no longer leaves the new episode's Transcribe button stuck on "Queuing…" / disabled.

Images are untouched; review the new prompts, then **⚡ Regenerate selected**.

## v1.0.359 — 2026-06-13

### Added — Scene Review: stale-image detection + select/approve from inside the preview

**Stale images are now flagged.** When you re-prompt a scene in Scene Plan (or edit + save its prompt in Scene Review) without re-rendering, the existing image is now *stale* — rendered from an older prompt. Scene Review surfaces this so you can refresh exactly those:
- An **⚠ corner flag** on the thumbnail + an **"⚠ stale — re-render"** badge on the row (and in the preview), for every image whose prompt has changed since it was rendered.
- A **"⚠ Select stale (N)"** button in the toolbar ticks all stale scenes in one click, then **⚡ Regenerate selected** re-renders them as one parallel job.
- How it works: the renderer now stamps each image with the prompt it was rendered from (`rendered_prompt` in `scene_plan.json`); a mismatch with the current `visual_prompt` = stale. **Only images rendered from this version on are tracked** — older images won't light up retroactively (no false alarms), but the next time you render or re-prompt them, staleness tracks correctly.

**Select for re-render without leaving the preview.** Previously, to pick scenes for a batch re-render you had to close the full-size preview, find the row, tick its checkbox, and re-open. Now there's a **"☐ Select for re-render"** toggle right in the preview's action row — and a keyboard shortcut **Shift+Y** to toggle it while flipping through scenes with ← / →. Pick as you review, then ⚡ Regenerate selected.

### Files
- `electron/server/models/types.ts` (`ScenePlanEntry.rendered_prompt`)
- `electron/server/generators/continuity-render.ts` + `electron/server/generators/scene-image.ts` (stamp `rendered_prompt` when writing `image_path`)
- `electron/server/routes/scene-review.ts` (compute + return per-scene `stale`)
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/scene-review.vue` (stale badges + "Select stale", in-preview select button + Shift+Y)

## v1.0.354 — 2026-06-13

### Changed — Video Assembly timeline: Target Duration removed + continuity-aware Step 3
Step 3 (Title & Timeline) of Video Assembly is reworked around how videos are actually built now.

- **Target Duration is gone.** The old "Auto (match audio) / Custom range" control padded every video (+30 s) or rolled a random length, which made no sense now that episodes loop still images sized to the audio. The video body now **always equals the narration** — no padding, no random range. Step 3 shows a read-only **Video Length** line instead of a control.
- **"After Narration Ends" now carries its own length.** Because the tail used to be sized by the Target-vs-narration gap (which no longer exists), each ending is now explicit: **Fade to Black** fades over its fade-duration, **Black Screen** / **Hold Last Scene** get their own length slider, and a new **Hard Cut** ends the moment the narration stops. (The legacy "Continue Cycling" option is retired — it now behaves like Hard Cut, and old presets still load.)
- **Continuity / transcript-timed projects hide Scene Recycling.** For formats where each scene holds for its own planned span (sentence-aligned continuity), the sleep-story seconds-per-scene / shuffle / per-scene-exclude controls don't apply — Step 3 now shows a short "transcript-timed" note in their place. **Scene Transitions and Scene Animation stay available for every format**, so continuity videos can finally use the transition + animation effects. Recycled formats are unchanged.

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/video.ts` (video body = narration + an explicit post-audio tail; `hard-cut` carries no tail)
- `electron/server/models/types.ts` (`PostAudioBehavior` adds `hard-cut`; `VideoPostAudio.tail_seconds`; request `duration` now optional/ignored)

## v1.0.348 — 2026-06-12

### Added — Whisper transcription can run across multiple Voice Studio Macs
Subtitle transcription was not concurrent for two separate reasons:

- The Story Studio job queue treated `subtitles_transcribe` as a singleton, so only one episode transcription could run at a time.
- The Voice Studio Whisper path picked the first ready endpoint instead of using the local-model least-busy pool, so multiple configured URLs were only a failover list, not a parallel pool.

Voice Studio subtitle jobs now get their own bounded queue group. When you enqueue transcription with 2-3 configured Voice Studio URLs that are reachable and have the selected Whisper model cached, different episodes can transcribe at the same time, one long STT request per Mac. A single ready URL stays serial, and OpenAI Whisper remains serial because it has no local server pool to distribute across.

## v1.0.347 — 2026-06-12

### Fixed — timestamp scene transitions no longer collapse the final video
Rendering a timestamp-planned episode through the full **Scenes** assembler could prepare every scene correctly, then collapse the intermediate video to only a few dozen seconds when scene transitions were enabled. The timestamp bridge made each scene clip use its exact `scene_plan.json` duration, but the xfade transition graph still assumed every input clip used one uniform `seconds_per_scene` length.

The transition builder now carries real per-scene durations through the concat/xfade plan, calculates xfade offsets from the actual accumulated clip length, and clamps the transition duration when a timestamp scene is shorter than the chosen transition. Short clips like `0.80s` now use a safe transition length instead of breaking the graph.

## v1.0.344 — 2026-06-12

### Added — re-roll a chosen SET of scenes in parallel across the Mac pool
Clicking **Regenerate** on scenes one-by-one in Scene Review queued a *separate* `continuity_render` job per scene — and that queue runs one job at a time, each rendering a single image on a single Mac. So with 6 machines you still got one-at-a-time. The 6-machine parallelism only ever kicked in *inside* one multi-scene render job.

Now you can re-roll a selection as **one** parallel job that the growable worker pool spreads across every online Mac:

- **☑ checkboxes** on each scene + **⚡ Regenerate selected (N)** — re-renders exactly the scenes you ticked, in parallel.
- **☑ Select unapproved** — tick every not-yet-approved scene at once (then trim if you like).
- **⚡ Regenerate all unapproved** — one-click parallel re-render of everything not yet approved.

Each runs as a single `continuity_render` job with the new `scene_ids` selection, so it uses the shared least-busy pool (and absorbs Macs that come online mid-render, per v1.0.341). Tip: the per-scene **Regenerate** button is still there for a quick single fix — but for several scenes, use the selection so they run concurrently instead of serially.

### Files

## v1.0.343 — 2026-06-12

### Fixed — "Rewrite with AI" in Scene Review now uses a text model + stays on-style
The in-preview **Rewrite with AI** button (v1.0.342) was passing the **image** model (e.g. `imagestudio:…`) to the prompt rewrite — which is an LLM task — so it failed slowly with "Unsupported model" and timed out. Two fixes:

- **Uses a real text model.** Scene Review now resolves the first usable LLM model (the same way the model picker does) for the rewrite, instead of the image model. The button is disabled with a clear hint if no text model is configured, and the endpoint now rejects image models up front with an **instant, clear error** (no more long timeout).
- **Keeps the channel art style.** The rewrite previously got no style guidance, so the LLM invented its own art direction and drifted off-style. It now falls back to the episode's **Style Bible** (the same text the renderer appends to every prompt), so the rewritten prompt matches the rendered look instead of fighting it.

## v1.0.341 — 2026-06-12

### Fixed — local image pool: machines that come online (or recover) mid-render now join automatically
For continuity-chain renders distributed across a pool of local Image Studio Macs, the pool is no longer frozen to whichever machines were online when the job started — **no more idle machines**:

- **A Mac you turn on mid-render now joins within ~20s.** The pool is built over *all* configured endpoints (offline ones pre-marked-down), and a periodic re-probe pulls newly-online Macs into rotation — and, in parallel mode, spins up an extra worker for each so they actually take work instead of sitting idle. Previously a continuity render took a one-time health snapshot at job start, so a machine you powered on later was locked out for the whole job.
- **A Mac that drops out and comes back rejoins.** This already worked via the 30s self-healing TTL; the re-probe now also brings a recovered Mac back into rotation **immediately** (new `markUp`) instead of waiting out the TTL.
- **Still one inference per Mac.** The worker pool never exceeds the live endpoint count, so it never doubles up requests on a single machine (no OOM risk). "Auto" concurrency can grow up to the full configured pool; an explicit concurrency stays a hard cap.

### Files
- `electron/server/lib/endpoint-pool.ts` (new `markUp` — return a recovered endpoint to rotation without waiting out the down-TTL)
- `electron/server/generators/continuity-render.ts` (build the pool over all configured endpoints + pre-markDown offline; growable worker pool with a 20s re-probe that absorbs Macs coming online mid-render)
- `electron/server/__tests__/endpoint-pool.test.ts` (markUp test)

## v1.0.337 — 2026-06-12

### Added — guide character appearance is now per-channel, and can be turned off
The selective-guide behaviour from v1.0.336 is no longer a baked-in 40% — it's a **per-project setting**. On the **Character Sheet** page (continuity hub), a **"Guide character appearance"** slider (0–100%, a channel default that saves instantly) controls how often the recurring guide is on screen:

- **0%** — no guide character at all (pure event / place / map / artifact imagery over narration), for channels that don't use one.
- **~40%** (default) — selective, so the guide stays special.
- **100%** — guide in every scene (the pre-v1.0.336 behaviour).

The Scene Planner reads it (`config.json` → `character_density`) and targets that mix; the continuity renderer keys off each scene's type as before. Works in **both** planning modes — single-pass lets the LLM classify to the target, and two-pass (local-model deterministic split) distributes the types with an even-spread accumulator so character scenes are scattered, not clustered. Projects that never set it keep the v1.0.336 default behaviour.

### Files
- `electron/server/services/scene-planner.ts` (density-driven cast guidance in the planner prompt; exported `assignDensityToUntagged` even-spread distributor)
- `electron/server/generators/scene-plan.ts` (reads `character_density` from project config; applies it to untagged scenes; logs the resulting cast)
- `electron/server/models/types.ts` (`ScenePlanRunOptions.character_density` + builder opt)
- `electron/server/services/project-manager.ts` (`character_density` in the safe config read shape)
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/character-sheet.vue` (Guide appearance slider → project config)
- `electron/server/__tests__/scene-planner-salvage.test.ts` (density-distribution tests)

### Performance — big projects (200–300+ episodes) load faster, and providers stop "going missing"
Four root-cause fixes for the slowdown on episode-heavy projects:

- **One folder walk instead of 300.** The episode list endpoint used to re-walk the whole project tree from the root for EVERY episode just to resolve its folder path — descending into every other episode's image folders along the way. On a 300-episode project that multiplied into hundreds of thousands of redundant directory reads per page load. It now builds the code→folder index in a single walk shared by all rows.
- **Duplicate scans collapse into one.** Opening several generator pages at once used to fire several full status sweeps in parallel. Identical concurrent requests now share one computation.
- **Voice/model dropdowns can't starve anymore.** The Voice Studio voices / engines / Whisper probes and the macOS voice list are now cached for 60s (10 min for macOS) with a last-known-good fallback: if a probe fails while the disk is busy, the dropdown shows the previous list (flagged stale) instead of going empty. That was the "missing providers" bug.
- **4× more filesystem threads.** Node's filesystem thread pool defaults to 4 threads; the status sweep saturated all of them, which is what made unrelated requests queue up behind it. The app now boots with 16.

### Added — mark any pipeline step as done by hand (for imported assets)
Under the episode picker on every generator page there's now a **Steps: N/M done** summary — expand it to see every pipeline step as a chip (✓ done / ○ pending). Steps auto-detect from files on disk; when you import a finished result from outside the app (legacy audio, a thumbnail made elsewhere), the step could stay "pending" forever with no way to close it. Now: **click the pending chip to mark it done by hand** (shown with a dashed ring + "manual"), click again to return to auto-detect. Format-specific steps (Research / Clips / Scene plan / Scene review) only appear where they apply. Also:

- Importing assets via the Import dialog now refreshes that episode's status immediately (no more stale "pending" until a manual refresh).
- In "Show all" mode the dropdown now marks episodes that have THIS page's step done (`✓`, or `✓ (manual)` for hand-marked) — previously only fully-finished episodes got a mark.

### Cleanup
- Removed unused `@fal-ai/client` dependency; archived executed one-off migration scripts to `scripts/archive/`; repo-root scratch files deleted and `test-results.txt` gitignored.

### Files
- `electron/server/routes/ideas.ts` (single-walk episode-dir index + in-flight request coalescing on `/episodes`)
- `electron/server/lib/ttl-cache.ts` (new — stale-while-revalidate TTL cache) + `electron/server/__tests__/ttl-cache.test.ts` (8 tests)
- `electron/server/routes/audio.ts` (SWR cache on voices/models/transcribe/macOS probes, `?refresh=1` bypass)
- `electron/boot-env.ts` (new — `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=16`, imported first in `electron/main.ts`)
- `electron/server/routes/projects.ts` (status-cache invalidation after asset import)
- `frontend/components/EpisodeSelector.vue` (step chips + manual mark-done + per-page ✓ suffix)

### Added — continuity videos: the guide character now appears SELECTIVELY, not in every scene
For continuity-chain videos built around an anchored character (e.g. Boundless's explorer boy), the guide no longer shows up in all ~80 shots. The scene planner now **classifies every scene** — `character` / `event` / `environment` / `map` / `artifact` — aiming for a mix of roughly **40% character, 35% event, 15% map/environment, 10% artifact**, so the guide stays special by appearing selectively.

- **Non-character scenes** (the event itself, a place, a map, an artifact) are planned **without** the character in their prompt, and the renderer **drops the character sheet / anchor / previous-render references** for them (keeping style + composition) and adds a "no people" negative — so the guide doesn't get img2img'd into a battle scene or a map.

## v1.0.335 — 2026-06-11

### Added — concurrent text generation (generate multiple episodes at once)
Script outline, chapter expansion, metadata, image prompts, and scene planning no longer run strictly one-at-a-time. A new **Settings → Performance → "Script & Text Generation Concurrency"** slider (1–8, default 2) controls how many of these text jobs run simultaneously **across all of them combined** — so you can kick off several episodes in parallel instead of watching them queue. Concurrent calls spread automatically across your LM Studio endpoint pool (the shared least-busy dispatcher), so more endpoints = more real speedup. Set it to roughly your number of endpoints; **1** = the old fully-serial behaviour.

Deliberately **unaffected**: image generation, video assembly, continuity render, audio, b-roll, and uploads still run one at a time — overlapping those would thrash the machine or trip provider rate limits. Concurrency is also strictly across **different episodes** (one episode still runs its own phases in order). It's a per-machine setting (reflects your local LM Studio capacity) and applies live without a restart.

### Files
- `electron/server/services/job-queue.ts` (per-type single slot → shared "llm" concurrency group with a configurable budget; new `pump`/`runJob`/`releaseSlot`/`pumpGroup`)
- `electron/server/services/app-settings.ts` (`script_concurrency` get/set + clamp 1–8)
- `electron/server/routes/app-settings.ts` (GET/PUT `/app-settings/script-concurrency`, applies to the live queue)
- `electron/server/boot/executors.ts` (load the saved value into the queue at boot)
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/settings.vue` (Performance slider + load/save alongside the other concurrency knobs)
- `electron/server/__tests__/job-queue-concurrency.test.ts` (new — shared-budget + serial-for-non-LLM invariants)

### Fixed — thumbnail prompts leaking into the script (chapters ending with "thumbnail prompts: 1. …")
Some generated chapters ended with a stray image/thumbnail prompt block — e.g. Capi's _Psychology of Release_ had `watercolor style, soft palette … thumbnail prompts: 1. A cracked mirror…` glued onto the end of Chapter 4, in a niche that uses oil-painting scenes and charcoal thumbnails (so "watercolor" obviously didn't belong).

**Root cause:** the default `production_standards.txt` that ships with new projects had an `## Image Prompts` section ("End every prompt with your preferred style tag, e.g. *watercolor style, soft palette*; generate 3-5 thumbnail prompts"). That whole file is folded into the **script-writing** system prompt — so the writing model occasionally followed those image instructions and appended thumbnail prompts inside a chapter. Image and thumbnail prompts already have their own dedicated generators; the script writer should never see those rules.

**The fix, three layers:**
- Removed the `## Image Prompts` section from both shipped templates (`blank`, `sleep-stories`) and rewrote the "customize your standards" helper to tell the LLM *not* to add image/thumbnail rules.
- Added a defensive strip in `systemPrompt()` — any `## Image Prompts` / `## Thumbnail…` H2 block is removed from a project's standards before they reach the script writer. This protects **existing** projects whose on-disk standards file still has the old section, with no per-project migration needed.
- Cleaned the affected on-disk file for the Capi project.

This only changes what the **script writer** sees — the real image/thumbnail generators are untouched and still read the niche's visual + thumbnail style sheets.

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/episode.ts` (`stripImagePromptSections()` + call in `systemPrompt()`)
- `electron/templates/blank/production_standards.txt`, `electron/templates/sleep-stories/production_standards.txt` (dropped the Image Prompts section)
- `electron/server/__tests__/strip-image-prompt-sections.test.ts` (new — 8 cases pinning the strip)

## v1.0.333 — 2026-06-11

### Added — Narration Volume control on the Audio Merge page
Reviewers can now flag the voiceover as "too soft" and you can actually fix it: the Audio Merge page has a new **Narration Volume** slider (50–200%, default 100% = unchanged) that sets the base loudness of the voiceover **only** — music, background noise, and ambient beds keep their own sliders and are untouched. Previously the narration level was hardcoded to 100% with no way to boost it. Above 130% without normalization, an inline warning suggests turning on Volume Normalization to avoid clipping. The value is saved/restored with audio-merge presets and shown in the pre-merge summary.

### Clarified — what Volume Normalization actually touches
For the record (no behavior change): **Volume Normalization only normalizes the narration chapters** to a consistent −16 LUFS (EBU R128) *before* mixing. Background music, noise, and ambient tracks are mixed in afterward at their own fixed volumes and are **never** normalized — so turning it on will not pump quiet ambient beds up to voiceover loudness.

A new built-in niche for contemplative, single-topic psychology video-essays — the "The Psychology of Effortless Charm" / "The Dark Side of Kindness" / "How Someone Slowly Goes Crazy" style. Modelled on real reference scripts:

## v1.0.329 — 2026-06-09

### Added — macOS built-in voices as a free TTS provider
New **"macOS say (built-in · free)"** audio provider that renders narration with the Mac's own voices — **local, free, offline, no API key, no rate limits, no per-character cost.** It's a normal provider in the audio model dropdown (treated exactly like ElevenLabs / fal / GenAIPro / Voice Studio), intended for **zero-cost preview renders** — hear a script's pacing before spending ElevenLabs credits, then swap to a premium provider for the final episode.

**How it works:** shells out to the system `say` command (AIFF) and transcodes to MP3 via the bundled ffmpeg — the same real-MP3 contract the rest of the pipeline expects. Per-chapter render + merge, identical to every other provider.

**Voices:** the picker auto-lists the renderable English voices via `say -v '?'`, best first — **Premium → Enhanced → base** — with the classic novelty voices (Bells, Boing, Zarvox, …) filtered out. Whatever Premium/Enhanced voices you download in **System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → System Voice → Manage Voices** appear automatically, no app update needed (e.g. Evan/Tom Enhanced, Jamie Premium). When Apple ships better voices in a future macOS update, they'll show up on their own too.

**Speed:** the existing audio **Speed** control maps to words-per-minute — 1.0× = a calm 150 wpm (sleep-story sweet spot), scaling from there. `say`'s own default (~175–200 wpm) is too fast for narration, so this anchors lower by default.

**Not exposed — the Siri voices.** They're licensed to the Siri assistant only; `say` silently falls back to the default voice when asked for them, so they're not renderable by any app (and using them in published content would be a licensing violation regardless). They simply don't appear in the picker.

### Files
- `electron/server/lib/macos-say-client.ts` (NEW) — voice listing (parse + tier + novelty filter), render (`say` → ffmpeg → MP3), speed→wpm.
- `electron/server/providers/audio/macos.ts` (NEW) — the `AudioProvider` (preview path); self-registers.
- `electron/server/boot/providers.ts` — register the provider.
- `electron/server/generators/audio.ts` — `macos` in the provider union, resolver, label, no-key branch, per-chunk render branch.
- `electron/server/models/types.ts` + `models/defaults.ts` — `macos` provider + the `macos-say` catalog entry ($0).
- `electron/server/routes/audio.ts` — resolver, `GET /macos/voices`, preview-voice branch.
- `frontend/composables/useModelGroups.ts` — provider grouping + display label.
- `frontend/components/VoicePicker.vue` — `macos-builtin` scope (reuses the local-voices section; fetches `/macos/voices`; stores the plain voice name).

## v1.0.326 — 2026-06-09

### Fixed — bogus `<project>/episodes/episodes/` empty directory created on linked projects whose folder is already named `episodes`

The user noticed `MineePod/episodes/episodes/` (empty) in their Downloads tree and asked where it came from. Investigation showed:

- Their MineePod project was registered via "Add existing project folder" pointing at `Downloads/.../MineePod/episodes/` (which itself contained a `.story-studio-project.json` from a prior iCloud sync).
- `getProjectDir('mineepod')` then returns that linked external directory (named literally `episodes`).
- `createProject` and `writeProjectFromInspection` both run `await fs.mkdir(path.join(projectDir, 'episodes'), { recursive: true })` as a defensive "episodes alias" — but never check whether `projectDir` is **already** named `episodes`. So the join produces `…/episodes/episodes/`, mkdir creates it empty, nothing ever fills it.

Fix: both call sites now skip the alias mkdir when the projectDir's basename is `episodes` (case-insensitive). The alias is just there so legacy code paths can do `path.join(projectDir, 'episodes')` without checking — when projectDir IS the episodes location, projectDir itself is the alias target, so nothing more needs creating.

This was the **mechanism** for the bogus dir on future imports. Existing trees (like the user's MineePod) still have the empty `episodes/episodes/` left over — see the new cleanup script for that.

### Added — `tools/cleanup-nested-episodes-dirs.mjs`: safe scan-and-clean for the bogus dirs

One-shot Node script that walks every registered project's directory tree, finds any directory matching the bogus pattern (`<projectDir>/episodes/` where `<projectDir>` is itself already named `episodes`, AND the dir is empty after filtering `.DS_Store`/`._*`), and shows you a delete plan. Dry-run by default — re-run with `--apply` to delete.

```
node tools/cleanup-nested-episodes-dirs.mjs            # dry-run
node tools/cleanup-nested-episodes-dirs.mjs --apply    # actually delete
```

It also compares duplicate `Season 001/EP*` directories between a project's outer wrapper and inner `episodes/` tree (the MineePod case) and reports which episodes have IDENTICAL content vs different — so you can confidently delete the dupe side without losing unique work.

### Files
- `electron/server/services/import-project.ts` — guard around `fs.mkdir(path.join(projectDir, 'episodes'))`.
- `electron/server/services/project-manager.ts` — same guard inside `createProject`.
- `tools/cleanup-nested-episodes-dirs.mjs` (new) — safe scan-and-clean script for existing trees.

### Verification
- Backend `tsc` clean; 1068 backend tests pass.

## v1.0.325 — 2026-06-09

### Changed — Kokoro dropdown labels now reflect real-world reliability

The user ran EP0003 cleanly on `voicestudio-kokoro-pt` (PyTorch) after the MLX 4-bit and bf16 variants each failed jobs under their actual workload (5 Macs × 3-parallel TTS). That's the empirical result from a real workload, not a benchmark — and it inverts the "MLX is the fast Apple Silicon choice" assumption I'd been working from.

What's true:
- **MLX 4-bit** is the fastest per-chunk on a single Mac, but mlx-audio's runtime stability degrades under concurrent load. Multi-chunk parallel jobs hit "didn't produce a wav file" glitches often enough to fail.
- **MLX bf16** has had download-incomplete + runtime issues on top of the same concurrency problem.
- **PyTorch** (`hexgrad/Kokoro-82M`) is the slowest per chunk but rock-solid reliable across the same pool.

The dropdown labels now lead with this trade-off:

| Old label | New label |
|---|---|
| Kokoro v1.0 82M (MLX 4-bit, recommended) | Kokoro v1.0 82M (MLX 4-bit — fastest, may glitch under heavy concurrent load) |
| Kokoro v1.0 82M (MLX bf16, full precision) | Kokoro v1.0 82M (MLX bf16 — full precision, has had download issues) |
| Kokoro v1.0 82M (PyTorch baseline) | Kokoro v1.0 82M (PyTorch — most reliable, slower per chunk) |

The default (`voicestudio-kokoro`) **stays at MLX 4-bit** — for a single-Mac or low-parallelism setup the speed is real value, and changing the default twice in 24 h would just be churn. **For pool users with parallelism, pick the PyTorch entry.**

Nothing else changed — pure label edit + behaviour comment in the source.

## v1.0.324 — 2026-06-09

### Fixed — "Failed to parse URL from http://m4…, http://m1…, …" when the pool exhausts mid-job

EP0003 ran with two distinct failure modes in the same job:

1. Two `mlx-audio didn't produce a wav file` failures on Chapter 04 — same runtime glitch the v1.0.320 failover catches per-chunk; on EP0003 it just ran out of healthy Macs before any one chunk succeeded.
2. Three `Failed to parse URL from http://m4…tail4e72cf…, http://m1…, http://vengthengs…, http://kt-271…, …` failures. **The "URL" in the error is the whole 12-Mac comma-separated endpoint list jammed into one URL field.**

(2) was a real bug in `runOnPool` itself. When all live endpoints get marked down mid-job (every Mac you tried failed with a failover-class error), `dispatcher.pick()` returns null. The old code did:

```ts
const ep = dispatcher.pick() ?? fallbackUrl   // ← bug
```

`fallbackUrl` is what the caller passes for the no-dispatcher (single endpoint) case. Audio + image callers pass the comma-separated `apiKey` there because that's how Voice Studio + Image Studio identify themselves. So once the pool emptied, the next chunk's "endpoint" became the entire URL list, the voicestudio HTTP layer tried to construct a URL from it, and the parser barfed with the user-visible "Failed to parse URL from …" string.

Fix: with a dispatcher present, `pick()` returning null means the pool is exhausted — break the loop cleanly and throw the last real error. **`fallbackUrl` is only used when there's no dispatcher at all (single-endpoint mode).** Same code path image gen used to live in before v1.0.306 — and now both image + audio go through this clean exit.

Also added: a friendly error when the pool was empty *before* any attempt (e.g. every endpoint disabled in Settings or marked down before the call). Was throwing `undefined` (useless stack). Now says `"All endpoints in the pool are unavailable. Check Settings → Local Models."`

### Why EP0003 ran out of Macs in the first place

The `mlx-audio didn't produce a wav file` runtime glitch is per-endpoint, per-attempt. With v1.0.318/320 failover treating it as failover-class, each occurrence marks one endpoint down with a 30 s TTL. EP0003 had 12 chunks in 3-parallel mode against 5 online Macs; 2 chunks hit the glitch on different Macs at roughly the same time, marking both down; subsequent chunks ran into a shrunken live pool; by the time several more came through, all 5 were temporarily marked down and the loop hit `pick() → null`. Pre-v1.0.324 the loop then smeared the apiKey into the endpoint slot. Post-fix it throws cleanly so the chunk just fails with the actual `mlx-audio didn't produce a wav file` error and the caller can retry later (or "Skip existing" picks them up on the next run).

If the underlying mlx-audio glitch keeps happening regularly, the 30 s TTL needs to be longer or the mlx-audio install on those Macs needs investigation — that's the real long-term fix and lives outside Story Studio. v1.0.324 just makes the failure mode honest.

### Files
- `electron/server/lib/endpoint-pool.ts` — `runOnPool` no longer falls back to `fallbackUrl` when a dispatcher is present and exhausted; cleaner empty-pool error.
- `electron/server/__tests__/endpoint-pool.test.ts` — 2 new tests covering the exact EP0003 scenario (callback must never receive the comma-list) + the empty-pool-before-attempt edge case.

### Verification
- Backend `tsc` clean; **1068 backend tests pass** (1066 + 2 new). The new EP0003 regression test passes `'http://a, http://b, http://c'` as the fallback and asserts the callback NEVER receives a string containing a comma — i.e. the exact symptom of the user's log can no longer happen.

## v1.0.321 — 2026-06-09

### Fixed — single-chunk retries always landed on the same broken Mac (the *real* EP0002 cause)

After v1.0.320 I expected the EP0002 Chapter 04 case to be solved — pool failover catches the `mlx-audio didn't produce a wav file` runtime error, marks down the glitched Mac, tries another. But the user retried 2-3 times and got the **same error every time**. That's not a transient glitch — that's the dispatcher's tie-break sending every retry to the same broken Mac.

Cause: `dispatcher.pick()` sorted candidates by in-flight count. When the pool is idle (all in-flight = 0) — which happens on every fresh single-chunk job — JavaScript's stable sort kept the original input order, so the first endpoint in your URL list won the tie every time. EP0002 Chapter 04 is exactly one chunk; the job creates a fresh dispatcher; the dispatcher always picks the same first endpoint; the same endpoint keeps failing.

Fix: **random tie-break.** When candidates have equal in-flight counts, `pick()` now randomises which one wins. Multi-chunk jobs are unaffected — the load-balancing kicks in as soon as one endpoint has 1 in-flight while others have 0. But single-chunk jobs (and any retry of a single-chunk job) now spread naturally across the pool.

Together with v1.0.320: even if EP0002 Chapter 04 keeps hitting `mlx-audio didn't produce a wav file` on some of your Macs, v1.0.321's random pick + v1.0.320's failover means **a healthy Mac eventually answers**, and the retry doesn't get stuck on the same broken one.

Verified the EP0002 Chapter 04 text directly (read the .md from disk) — pure English prose, no exotic characters, well within the chunk cap. Nothing about the *content* should crash mlx-audio. The failure is environmental on one or more Macs.

### Files
- `electron/server/lib/endpoint-pool.ts` — `pick()` now uses `Math.random() < 0.5` as the tie-break when in-flight counts are equal.
- `electron/server/__tests__/endpoint-pool.test.ts` — existing pick test updated (no longer asserts deterministic first endpoint); new statistical test runs 200 fresh-dispatcher single-picks across 5 endpoints and asserts each is picked at least 10 times (would have failed pre-v1.0.321 with 200 to one endpoint and 0 to the others).

### Verification
- Backend `tsc` clean; **1066 backend tests pass** (1065 + 1 new statistical test).

### Followup: why is mlx-audio failing on those Macs in the first place?
v1.0.321 routes around the symptom but doesn't fix the underlying mlx-audio glitch. If a specific Mac keeps failing every time the random tie-break sends a chunk its way, that Mac has a real local issue — check Voice Studio's own logs on that machine. Likely candidates: Voice Studio version mismatch with the bf16 weights, MPS memory pressure from another app, mlx-audio package needing a reinstall on that machine. From Story Studio's side, there's not much more we can do.

## v1.0.320 — 2026-06-09

### Fixed — pool fails over on the "mlx-audio didn't produce a wav file" runtime (the EP0002 case)

After yesterday's Kokoro MLX download finished on all your Macs, a TN0002/EP0002 chapter still failed — but with a different error this time:

> `Voice Studio job failed: RuntimeError: mlx-audio didn't produce a wav file. Temp dir: /var/folders/.../mlxaudio_kokoro-mlx_*`

The endpoint was alive, the model was loaded, the inference even started — but on **one** of your 5 online Macs, mlx-audio failed mid-generation and didn't write the wav. The same chunk would have rendered fine on any of the other 4 Macs (identical code, same model file). v1.0.318's failover only matched "not fully cached" and "no models loaded" — this *runtime* failure flavour wasn't caught, so the chunk died on the one glitched Mac instead of moving to a healthy one.

New `isInferenceFailureError` matcher catches:
- `"didn't produce a wav file"` / `"did not produce a wav"` — the EP0002 case
- `"produced no output"` / `"no audio produced"` / `"wav file not found"` — likely close relatives
- `"failed to generate audio"` — generic Voice Studio "the job tried and failed" phrasing
- `"mlx-audio … RuntimeError"` either ordering

…and joins `isConnectionError` + `isModelNotReadyError` under `isFailoverableError`. So runOnPool now treats *transport problems*, *missing-model problems*, and *inference glitches* the same way: mark the offending endpoint down, fail over to a healthy one. The standard 30 s self-healing TTL means the glitched Mac re-enters the pool on the next chunk, in case its hiccup was a one-off (which mlx-audio runtime errors usually are).

Deliberately **not** matched: bare `RuntimeError` (too broad — a malformed prompt or unsupported voice that genuinely fails everywhere shouldn't waste retries through every Mac). If a new flavour shows up that should fail over, add it to the matcher.

### Files
- `electron/server/lib/endpoint-pool.ts` — `isInferenceFailureError` matcher + folded into `isFailoverableError`.
- `electron/server/__tests__/endpoint-pool.test.ts` — 3 new tests, including the exact EP0002 RuntimeError string as a regression guard, plus a negative-match suite for true content errors that should still NOT fail over.

### Verification
- Backend `tsc` clean; **1065 backend tests pass** (1062 + 3 new). The new "EP0002 runtime" test reproduces the failure end-to-end through `runOnPool` — one Mac throws the verbatim error string, the second succeeds, the chunk lands on the healthy Mac, and the glitched one gets marked down.

### Followup
The deeper "why did mlx-audio fail on that Mac" is a Voice Studio / mlx-audio question I can't fix from this side — could be memory pressure, an MPS hiccup, a transient model-load bug. If the SAME Mac keeps failing across many runs, check Voice Studio's own logs on that machine. The pool just routes around it cleanly so your job doesn't suffer.

## v1.0.319 — 2026-06-08

### Fixed — default Kokoro repo switched to MLX bf16 (matches what's actually downloaded on Apple Silicon)

Followup to v1.0.318. Diagnosing the user's "all my servers have the model" report against `vengthengs-mac-mini` revealed something important: Voice Studio's `kokoro_available: true` flag means *"the Kokoro engine is importable"*, NOT *"the specific repo we asked for is cached"*. Story Studio was sending `repo: 'hexgrad/Kokoro-82M'` (PyTorch baseline) — but the Mac actually had `mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16` cached (the MLX variant most users download via the Voice Studio Models tab on Apple Silicon). Same engine, same audio quality, different weight files; the 409 was Voice Studio honestly reporting *"that specific repo isn't on disk."*

The user confirmed: the green "Downloaded" badge in their Voice Studio Models tab is on `mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16`, not hexgrad. So Story Studio's default Kokoro repo is now that one — the one their Macs actually have. Going forward, fresh Voice Studio installs on Apple Silicon will Just Work without anyone having to manually download a second variant.

- Same `voice` field (Kokoro voicepacks like `af_bella` work across both repos).
- Same `/api/generate/txt2speech` endpoint.
- `kokoro_available` covers both — no separate `kokoro_mlx_available` flag exists in the catalog.
- The label updated to `"Kokoro v1.0 82M (MLX bf16)"` so the variant is visible in the model dropdown.

If anyone specifically wanted the PyTorch baseline: download `hexgrad/Kokoro-82M` from the Voice Studio Models tab and v1.0.318's pool failover routes around any Mac that doesn't have it.

### Why this wasn't a v1.0.318 fix
v1.0.318 makes mixed-cache setups work via failover — your existing 2-of-5 setup (2 Macs with hexgrad, 3 without) would have rendered fine after that release because all chunks would have ended up on the 2 hexgrad Macs. This release goes further by aligning the default with what's actually downloaded, so all 5 Macs work instead of just the 2.

### Files
- `electron/server/lib/voicestudio-client.ts` — `voicestudio-kokoro` engine entry's `repo` field switched from `hexgrad/Kokoro-82M` to `mlx-community/Kokoro-82M-bf16`. Family stays `kokoro` (single availability flag). Label updated to disclose the variant.

## v1.0.318 — 2026-06-08

### Fixed — pool now fails over when a Mac is alive but missing the model (the TN1611 Kokoro case)

You ran an EP0001 audio gen on Kokoro across 12 Voice Studio Macs (5 online). 2 of those 5 had the Kokoro model loaded, the other 3 didn't, and the 3 that didn't returned `409: Model hexgrad/Kokoro-82M is not fully cached`. Every chunk that landed on one of those 3 Macs **died** instead of being retried on the 2 that worked. You got 8 failures and 2 successes — exactly the math the pool's behaviour produced.

This was a real gap. The pool's failover-or-fail decision was: connection error → fail over; anything else → real content error, no failover. A `409 not fully cached` is neither: it's a **per-endpoint capability error** — the Mac is alive and reachable, just doesn't have the model. Failing over to a different Mac in the same pool is the correct response, and the v1.0.295 comment in the LM Studio provider that said "the user keeps the same models loaded everywhere" no longer holds for your real setup.

What's now fixed:

- A new `isModelNotReadyError` matcher catches `"not fully cached"`, `"no models loaded"`, `"model_not_found"`, `"has no model … loaded"`, and the polite variants providers wrap them in.
- The dispatcher's failover decision is now `isFailoverableError = connection-error OR model-not-ready`. Same rules as before — least-busy pick, mark-down on failure, try the next live one — just with model-not-ready added to "failure."
- The existing **30-second self-healing TTL** on marked-down endpoints unchanged — the same mechanism that re-enters a sleeping Mac after it wakes up also re-enters one whose model just finished downloading. So your *"once I restore the server, it auto-rejoins the pool"* expectation now works for the model-not-loaded case too.

For your EP0001 setup, the new flow:
- Chunk 1 → dispatcher → picks one of the 3 missing-Kokoro Macs → 409 → mark down → tries another → maybe another miss → mark down → lands on a Kokoro-loaded Mac → **success**.
- After a few markdowns, only the 2 loaded Macs are eligible; all remaining chunks succeed on them.
- 30 s later, the marked-down Macs become eligible again. If they're still missing the model (you haven't downloaded it), they fail once more and get re-marked. If you've downloaded it in the meantime, they rejoin and start serving traffic. Self-healing.

The LM Studio provider's "has no model loaded" wrap message was also updated — it used to say *"Load it on every endpoint in your pool"*, which was misleading because the user there had told us they always do. Now it says *"failing over to another endpoint in the pool"*, accurate for the multi-model-availability case.

### Files
- `electron/server/lib/endpoint-pool.ts` — `isModelNotReadyError` + `isFailoverableError`; `runOnPool` now uses `isFailoverableError` instead of `isConnectionError` directly.
- `electron/server/providers/text/lmstudio.ts` — friendly-wrap message updated to mention failover.
- `electron/server/__tests__/endpoint-pool.test.ts` — 5 new tests covering the exact TN1611 Kokoro scenario (3 missing-model endpoints + 1 loaded) + the LM Studio variant + the union semantics.

### Verification
- Backend `tsc` clean; **1062 backend tests pass** (1057 + 5 new). The new "TN1611 Kokoro" test reproduces the exact symptom (Voice Studio 409 with the "not fully cached" body) and proves the chunk now succeeds on the loaded endpoint.
- Pure additive change to the public API (new exports `isModelNotReadyError` + `isFailoverableError`); existing `isConnectionError` semantics unchanged.

## v1.0.317 — 2026-06-08

### Added — Per-chunk pause (Audio Assembly) — fixes the rushed-robotic feel on cloud TTS chunked chapters

When a long chapter goes over the TTS char cap, the audio generator splits it into `_part1`, `_part2`, … and Audio Assembly concatenates them back into one chapter. Until now those parts were joined **back-to-back** — and because cloud TTS (ElevenLabs, GenAIPro, fal) chunks end and start mid-breath, the seam sounds rushed and artificial. The longer the chapter, the more obvious it gets.

There's now a **Per-chunk pause** slider on the Audio Assembly page that inserts a small silence (0.0 – 3.0s) between every `_partN` transition within the same chapter. Default is **0s** (current/legacy behaviour, no surprise on existing projects). Try **0.3–1s** for a natural breath. Different-chapter transitions still use the existing **Silence Between Chapters** value — they're independent controls.

The slider only appears when the loaded episode actually has multi-part chapters (so it doesn't clutter the UI on episodes that fit in one chunk per chapter). The summary line at the top of the page shows the math: total narration + chapter gaps + chunk pauses = estimated duration.

Important: the per-chapter duration sidecar (`audio_chapters.json`) folds the inter-part silences into each chapter's duration so per-chapter SRT cues stay aligned with the merged audio. Without this the subtitles would drift by `(parts−1) × chunk_silence` for every multi-part chapter (~11 seconds on a 23-part chapter at 0.5s pauses — substantial).

### On the "is ffmpeg overloaded?" concern

Your TN0161 merge with 171 chunks succeeded and produced a clean 39m file. The merge step concatenates fine at that scale — ffmpeg eats hundreds of files in one pass with no issue. The reliability worry was actually upstream: the per-file `ffprobe` spawn loop briefly stalls the event loop, which used to time out the projects fetch on the home page. **That was fixed in v1.0.316** with the projects auto-retry. The deeper fix — running the probes in batches with a concurrency cap so the event loop never gets starved — is still filed as a followup for a focused future release.

On the "two-stage merge" idea (stitch chunks → chapter files → episode): considered and rejected as a separate step. The new `chunk_silence_sec` parameter on the existing single-stage merge gives the same audible result (a chapter with natural breathing between its parts) without introducing intermediate files to track / clean up / keep in sync with regenerations. One ffmpeg pass, same output.

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/audio-merge.ts` — `chunk_silence_sec` handling: builds a second ffmpeg silence track, inserts it between same-chapter parts in the concat list, folds inter-part silences into the sidecar's per-chapter duration so subtitles stay aligned.
- `electron/server/models/types.ts` — `chunk_silence_sec?: number` added to `AudioMergeRequest`.
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/audio-merge.vue` — new "Per-chunk pause" slider gated on `hasMultiPartChapters`; chunk/chapter transition counts; updated summary bar; preset save/apply for the new field.

### Verification
- Backend `tsc` clean; **1057 backend tests pass** (no test changes — the new path is exercised when the field is set, and the legacy path is byte-for-byte identical when it's absent or 0).
- `nuxt generate` build compiles every SFC. Frontend behaviour is gated correctly: the slider only appears for episodes with `_partN` files; the summary bar shows the new contribution only when `chunkSilenceSec > 0 AND chunkTransitions > 0`.

## v1.0.316 — 2026-06-08

### Fixed — projects list no longer goes blank when a big job is running

What kept happening: while an audio merge or image batch was in flight, navigating to the home page (or reloading) sometimes showed "no projects" — a forever-empty Welcome screen — until you hit ⌘R manually. Even though the projects, jobs, and data were all fine on disk.

Why: the merge job's per-file `ffprobe` / `ffmpeg` spawns keep the Node event loop very busy for short bursts. A request from the renderer that lands in a bad ~200ms window can time out. The home page's projects fetch was **one-shot** — if it failed, it set `projects = []` and stayed that way. The empty array then rendered as "you have no projects" since nothing distinguished "fetch failed" from "genuinely empty."

Fix (two parts):

1. **Auto-retry with backoff** on the projects fetch: 1 try + 3 retries at 1s / 3s / 9s. A 200ms backend hiccup is invisible to you — the first retry succeeds and the list renders normally. Worst case (4 failures = 13s) the page shows a manual recovery option:
2. **A "Couldn't load your projects — Retry" panel**, distinct from the Welcome onboarding card. One click re-runs the same retry sequence. Your projects + data + jobs are untouched on disk; this is purely about the UI re-asking the backend.

So a brief backend stall during a merge job no longer leaves the home page stranded.

### Files
- `frontend/pages/index.vue` — `fetchProjectsWithRetry()` helper with 1/3/9-second backoff; `projectsLoadError` sticky error state; a new "Couldn't load" panel + Retry button rendered when the error is set (vs. the Welcome card for genuine first-run empty).

### Verification
- `nuxt generate` build compiles every SFC. The retry helper uses `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, …))` between attempts, so it doesn't busy-wait. The error state is cleared on any success (including a legitimate empty array), so the Welcome onboarding still renders on a fresh install.

### Followups (not in this release)
The deeper cause is the merge job's event-loop pressure during heavy ffprobe spawning. The right fix is to batch / parallelize those probes with a concurrency cap (say 4 at a time) so the burst never starves the HTTP server in the first place. Filed for a future release.

## v1.0.315 — 2026-06-08

### Fixed — Audio Assembly: parts of the same chapter now sort numerically (part2 before part10)

On a chapter that got split into many TTS chunks (e.g. TN0153's Chapter 04 with 23 parts from yesterday's broken-cap run), the Audio Assembly list — and the actual merge order — sorted **alphabetically** within the chapter: `part1, part10, part11, part12, …, part19, part2, part20, …`. That meant the stitched audio would have been in the wrong order, doubly so on a re-merge: the parts you already generated weren't being wasted, but they were being concatenated jumbled.

The comparator now does a proper natural sort for `_partN` suffixes: `part1, part2, part3, …, part10, …, part23`. A **bare** chapter file (no `_partN`, e.g. an imported single-file render of that chapter) sorts before its parts — so if both exist the bare one is picked up first by the merge step. Introduction → Chapter_01..N → bare chapter → parts.

The merge step itself already grouped same-key files together (the parts of one chapter never get a silence gap inserted between them — that's the `chapterKeyOf` logic from v1.0.224). The fix here is only the within-chapter ordering.

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/audio-merge.ts` — extracted `compareChapterFilenames` (now exported) and added the same-chapter tiebreak that orders `_partN` numerically; `scanEpisodeAudioAssets` calls the helper.
- `electron/server/__tests__/chapter-part-grouping.test.ts` — 6 new tests, including the exact TN0153 shape (Intro + 1-3 + bare Chapter_04 + 23 parts) as a regression guard.

### Verification
- Backend `tsc` clean; **1057 backend tests pass** (1051 baseline + 6 new sort tests). One of them sorts the exact 23-part TN0153 layout from your screenshot and asserts the natural order. No frontend changes — the Assembly UI reads from the backend scan, so this single fix corrects both the displayed list and the actual merge concat order.

## v1.0.313 — 2026-06-08

### Fixed — cloud TTS chunked at 250 chars (the "Chunk cap: 250 chars" + 5-minute timeout)

What you saw on TN0153: a cloud model (GenAIPro Multilingual v2) chunked at **250 chars per submit** — slicing the Introduction into 10 parts and Chapter 04 into 23 — then timed out after 5 minutes. The log even called it out: *"per-job override from the Audio page; default would have been unset"*.

What happened: the Audio page has a **Max chunk size** field gated to Voice Studio (local cloning engines need tiny chunks). If you'd set a value while on a Voice Studio model and then switched to a cloud model, the input disappeared from the screen — but the value **stayed in form state** and shipped through to the backend on the next submit, capping the cloud run at the local-sized 250. The submit-time strip checked only "is it a positive number?", not "are we even on a local provider?"

Now the strip checks the provider. The value is also cleared automatically when you switch off Voice Studio, so it can't sneak into a saved preset.

### Added — per-model chunk-size cap in Settings → Audio Models

You asked: *"why don't I get a per-model chunk control? different voices have different limits, so I can have it saved."* That's exactly the right shape — and the backend already supported it (`AudioModelConfig.tts_soft_max_chars`), there just wasn't a Settings UI for it.

A new **Max chunk chars** column on the **Audio Model Pricing** table now lets you set the per-model cap. Leave it blank to use the chunker default (≈4800). Suggested values:

- **ElevenLabs / GenAIPro / fal proxies** → 3000–4800 (paste what their docs allow for your tier).
- **Voice Studio Kokoro** → 3000+ (no cloning drift).
- **VoxCPM2** → 500–600 (cloned voice drifts after ~30s).
- **Chatterbox** → 1000 (drifts after ~60s).

The per-job override on the Audio page is now strictly an *escape hatch for Voice Studio*; the per-model setting in Settings is the everyday control.

### Files
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/audio.vue` — submit-time strip now gates on `currentAudioProvider !== 'voicestudio'`; new watcher clears `form.max_chunk_chars` when switching off Voice Studio.
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/settings.vue` — new **Max chunk chars** column on the Audio Models table; save handler normalizes empty/NaN to "unset" so blank means "use the chunker default."

### Verification
- `nuxt generate` build compiles every SFC. The backend already reads `tts_soft_max_chars` from `audio_models` config (see `generators/audio.ts` modelEntry handling) so no backend change was needed — only the UI to set it and the bug-stop to keep the local-only override from leaking.

## v1.0.311 — 2026-06-08

### Added — On/Off switch per local endpoint (skip the Macs you know are off)

Each Mac in your local pools (LM Studio / Image Studio / Voice Studio) now has an **On / Off** toggle in **Settings → Local Models**. Switch one **Off** and the app treats it as if it weren't there:

- **Never sent work** — generation only dispatches across the **On** endpoints.

(At least one endpoint must stay On; the single per-row **Test** button still works on an Off endpoint if you want to check it before switching it back on.)

Why: on a channel running many Macs, some are coworkers' machines that aren't on every day (weekends, variable schedules), and probing a powered-down or busy Mac just wastes time and risks dipping into CPU someone else needs.

## v1.0.309 — 2026-06-08

### Fixed — Retry on Image Prompts now fills only the gaps (instead of redoing all of them)

When an Image Prompts job partially failed — e.g. *"Generated 90 of 100 scene prompts — 10 scenes missing: 11-20"* — clicking **Retry** used to regenerate **all 100 from scratch** and overwrite the file, despite the message saying "fill the gaps." That wasted time (and money, on cloud models), and replaced the prompts you already had with different ones — which would then no longer match any scene images you'd made from them.

**Retry is now smart.** It reads the prompts already on disk, regenerates **only the missing scenes** (e.g. just batch 11–20), and **merges** them back in — keeping the ones that already succeeded. Thumbnails are left untouched if they're already there. So a 10-scene gap costs one ~30-second batch, not a full 100-scene re-run. It works across a page reload too, since it reads from disk rather than job memory.

This was the one job type that didn't already do the right thing. For reference, here's how each Retry behaves:

- **Images / Audio / AI Video** — already smart: a free **Repair** button recovers in-flight work from the provider, and Retry skips anything already on disk (only re-renders what's missing). Unchanged.
- **Image Prompts** — now fills only the missing scenes (this fix).
- **Metadata / Scripts / Merge / Assembly / Subtitles** — single-artifact steps; Retry re-runs the whole thing (no partial concept).

The **Retry** button's tooltip is now honest per job type (e.g. Image Prompts reads "SMART RETRY — regenerates only the missing scenes… cloud models charge only for the missing ones").

### Files
- `electron/server/generators/image-prompts.ts` — `fill_gaps` mode: load existing prompts, run only the batches with a missing scene, merge + preserve the rest. Full regeneration (the page's Generate button) is unchanged.
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/jobs.vue` — Image Prompts Retry routes to `/generate/image-prompts` with `fill_gaps=true`; type-aware Retry tooltip.

### Verification
- Backend `tsc` clean; all 1049 backend tests pass; jobs page SSR-renders clean. Verified the prompt parser + path resolution against the real on-disk TN0161 file (reads scenes back correctly), and that retried jobs carry the episode title needed to find the file. Full-regeneration path is byte-for-byte unchanged when `fill_gaps` is absent.

## v1.0.307 — 2026-06-08

### Fixed — Generate buttons now grey out while a job is running

Once you kicked off a render, the **Generate** button went live again the instant the job was *queued* — not when it actually *finished*. So a long scene-image or audio run looked idle, and it was easy to click Generate again (and again) thinking nothing had happened, stacking up duplicate jobs.

Every generator's Generate button now stays **disabled with a spinner** for the whole job — start to finish — and re-enables only when the queue is actually clear for that episode. This now reads straight from the job queue, so it's correct even if you **reload the page** mid-render or launched the job from a different button.

Fixed across the board so it behaves the same everywhere:

- **Scene & Thumbnail Generator** — both the top *Generate* button and the in-page *Generate All N* button (scene and thumbnail stay independent — you can still queue thumbnails while scenes render).
- **Image Prompts, Script, Audio, Audio Merge, Video, Video Assembly** generators.
- **Research, Scene Plan, Scene Review, Timestamp Assemble**, and B-roll *Assemble video*.

(Metadata and Subtitles already behaved this way. Pipeline is unchanged — it's a multi-episode batch behind a confirm dialog, so re-running queues a fresh batch on purpose.)

### Files
- `frontend/composables/useJobs.ts` — new shared `isJobActiveFor(episodeId, types)` helper: the one authoritative "is a job in-flight for this episode?" check.
- `frontend/pages/projects/[slug]/{images,image-prompts,audio,audio-merge,scripts,video,video-assembly,broll,research,scene-plan,scene-review,timestamp-assemble}.vue` + `frontend/components/ImageGeneratorPanel.vue` — every Generate button now reflects the live job.

### Verification
- All 12 edited pages SSR-render cleanly (full `setup()` + computed evaluation, no TDZ/reference errors); dev log clean. The new helper generalizes the existing per-page checks that already shipped working on Metadata/Subtitles.

## v1.0.306 — 2026-06-08

### Fixed — local image generation now uses your whole fleet of Macs

If you run Image Studio on several Macs, image + thumbnail generation was only ever using **one** of them — it crawled through everything serially. Two bugs were behind it:

- **It treated your whole endpoint list as a single broken URL** ("Failed to parse URL from …"). The image provider now parses the list into a pool and submits + polls on one Mac at a time, **failing over to a healthy Mac** on a connection error (the same treatment the local-LLM path got in 1.0.305).
- **It hard-clamped concurrency to 1.** Now it probes your endpoints and renders **across every healthy Mac in parallel** (each Mac runs one inference at a time; different Macs run at once). With 5 reachable Macs, 5 images render simultaneously — roughly 5× faster. You'll see *"Local modal pool: 5/12 reachable — concurrency=5"* in the job log.
- **Hanging Macs are skipped fast.** A Mac that's asleep-but-on-the-network used to stall a render for ~30s; a 4s pre-flight probe now skips it and moves on.

Queuing a thumbnail job and a scene job at the same time is safe — they share the same least-busy pool, so the load spreads evenly across your Macs and each Mac queues its own work.

### Fixed — model dropdown no longer empties when your Macs are busy

The local model picker did a live probe on every open; while every Mac was mid-render, the probe timed out and the dropdown went blank. It now **caches the last good catalog** (and tries several endpoints), so the list stays put through a busy batch. Refresh still forces a live re-check.

### Fixed — image Repair is split per pool

On the **Thumbnail Generator**, "Image integrity / Repair missing" now shows and repairs **thumbnails only**; on the **Scene Generator**, **scenes only**. No more combined "Repair missing (35)" mixing both halves. (The zero-cost provider-history recovery is unchanged.)

### Fixed — quality-of-life

- **Model & voice dropdowns close on outside-click** (and Escape) — no more re-clicking the field to dismiss them.
- **Number fields accept typed values again.** Speed / stability / similarity (and any slider-with-number field) snapped to a junk value while you typed; they now hold exactly what you type and clamp to range on blur.

### Files
- `electron/server/providers/image/imagestudio.ts` + `lib/imagestudio-client.ts` — endpoint pool + pre-flight probe.
- `electron/server/generators/images.ts` — parallel-across-Macs concurrency.
- `electron/server/routes/images.ts` — cached image-model list; per-pool repair.
- `electron/server/services/image-reconciler.ts` + `boot/executors.ts` — pool-scoped repair.
- `frontend/components/{ImageModelPicker,VoicePicker,SliderWithNumber}.vue`, `pages/projects/[slug]/images.vue` — dropdown dismiss, number-field fix, per-pool integrity card.

### Verification
- `tsc` clean; endpoint-pool 8/8, providers 18/18, format-loader 30/30. Parallel concurrency verified against the real fleet (12 endpoints → 5 healthy → concurrency 5) and in the live job log.

## v1.0.305 — 2026-06-07

### Fixed — local LLM generation no longer freezes when a Mac is asleep

When one of your LM Studio endpoints was unreachable (a Mac asleep or off Tailscale), generation could **freeze for ~5 minutes** and cancelling did nothing, because a sleeping Mac *hangs* the connection instead of refusing it — and the request had no timeout (10-minute default × 3 silent retries). This release makes the whole local-LLM path resilient:

- **Fast fail-fast + failover.** Every LM Studio request now does a quick reachability check first; an unreachable endpoint is detected in seconds and the work **fails over to a healthy Mac** instead of hanging. Requests are now bounded by a real timeout with no silent retries, so cancel is instant again.
- **Self-healing endpoint pool.** A Mac marked "down" after a blip now **rejoins automatically** after 30s (it used to stay excluded until restart). And `EHOSTUNREACH` — the exact error a sleeping Mac throws — now correctly triggers failover (it was slipping through before).
- **Scene-prompt batches retry and report honestly.** A failed batch now **retries up to 3×** (routing to a healthy endpoint). And a partial run no longer lies: instead of printing "Done." with 30 of 100 scenes, the job reports the exact shortfall (which batches failed, how many scenes are missing) — your generated scenes are saved, and you can re-run to fill only the gaps.
- **Model dropdown no longer empties.** The local-model list now unions models across **all** your endpoints, so a single sleeping Mac doesn't make every local model vanish from the picker.

### Files
- `electron/server/providers/text/lmstudio.ts` — pre-flight probe + request timeout + `maxRetries: 0`.
- `electron/server/lib/endpoint-pool.ts` — self-healing down-state TTL; `isConnectionError` aligned (incl. `EHOSTUNREACH`).
- `electron/server/lib/lmstudio-client.ts` + `routes/health.ts` + `routes/lmstudio.ts` — pooled model list across all endpoints.
- `electron/server/generators/image-prompts.ts` — per-batch retry + honest partial-completion reporting.

### Verification
- New `endpoint-pool.test.ts` (8/8): failover on connection error, no-failover on content error, `EHOSTUNREACH` matching, least-busy pick. Providers 18/18, `tsc` clean, backend boots.
